content: As a boy, Samuel served the LORD under which priest?
explanation: Samuel grew up in the house of the LORD. “And the boy Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli.” (1 Samuel 3:1, BSB)

content: When the LORD first called young Samuel at night, what did Samuel answer?
explanation: Samuel was ready to listen. “Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he answered, “Here I am.”” (1 Samuel 3:4, BSB)

content: When young Samuel heard his name called at night, who did he think was calling?
explanation: He did not yet know the LORD's voice. “He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.”” (1 Samuel 3:5, BSB)

content: How many times did the LORD call young Samuel before Eli realized it was God?
explanation: Then Eli knew the LORD was calling the boy. “Once again, for the third time, the LORD called to Samuel.” (1 Samuel 3:8, BSB)

content: What did Eli tell young Samuel to say if God called him again?
options: Speak, LORD, Your servant is listening
explanation: Samuel learned to listen to God. “Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.” (1 Samuel 3:9, BSB)

content: Where was young Samuel lying down when God called him?
options: In the temple of the LORD
explanation: The ark of God was there. “Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was located.” (1 Samuel 3:3, BSB)

content: As Samuel grew up, what did all Israel come to know about him?
explanation: The LORD was with Samuel. “knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.” (1 Samuel 3:20, BSB)

content: After God rejected King Saul, to whose family did He send Samuel to find a new king?
explanation: God had chosen a king from Jesse's sons. “I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem” (1 Samuel 16:1, BSB)

content: When Samuel was impressed by Jesse's tall son, what did God say He looks at?
explanation: People judge by looks, but God sees inside. “For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7, BSB)

content: How many of Jesse's sons passed before Samuel without being chosen?
explanation: The LORD had not chosen any of them. “Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel” (1 Samuel 16:10, BSB)

content: When Samuel came to anoint a new king, where was Jesse's youngest son?
explanation: No one thought the youngest would be chosen. ““There is still the youngest,” Jesse replied, “but he is tending the sheep.”” (1 Samuel 16:11, BSB)

content: What did Samuel use to anoint young David?
explanation: He anointed David in front of his brothers. “So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers” (1 Samuel 16:13, BSB)

content: After Samuel anointed David, what came upon him?
explanation: From that day God's Spirit was with David. “and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward.” (1 Samuel 16:13, BSB)

content: When King Saul was troubled, what instrument did young David play for him?
explanation: Saul felt better when David played. “David would pick up his harp and play” (1 Samuel 16:23, BSB)

content: Which Philistine champion challenged the army of Israel?
explanation: He was a giant warrior from Gath. “Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out from the Philistine camp.” (1 Samuel 17:4, BSB)

content: When Goliath shouted his challenge, how did Saul and the Israelites feel?
explanation: No one wanted to fight the giant. “Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and greatly afraid.” (1 Samuel 17:11, BSB)

content: Before facing Goliath, which wild animals did David say he had fought while keeping sheep?
explanation: God had already helped David against them. “and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock” (1 Samuel 17:34, BSB)

content: Why did David take off King Saul's armor before facing Goliath?
options: He was not used to it
explanation: David trusted God, not armor. “I am not accustomed to them.” (1 Samuel 17:39, BSB)

content: How many smooth stones did David choose from the brook before facing Goliath?
explanation: He put them in his shepherd's bag. “selected five smooth stones from the brook” (1 Samuel 17:40, BSB)

content: Facing Goliath, in whose name did David say he came?
explanation: Goliath had defied the living God. “but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts” (1 Samuel 17:45, BSB)

content: Where did David's stone hit Goliath?
explanation: The giant fell facedown. “striking the Philistine on the forehead.” (1 Samuel 17:49, BSB)

content: With what did young David defeat Goliath?
explanation: God gave the victory without a sword in David's hand. “Thus David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone” (1 Samuel 17:50, BSB)

content: After David defeated Goliath, whose soul became knit together with David's?
explanation: Jonathan, Saul's son, loved David as himself. “the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together” (1 Samuel 18:1, BSB)

content: Why did Jonathan make a covenant with David?
explanation: They became best friends. “Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.” (1 Samuel 18:3, BSB)

content: What did Jonathan give David as a sign of their friendship?
explanation: He also gave David his tunic and belt. “And Jonathan removed the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt.” (1 Samuel 18:4, BSB)

content: What song of the women made King Saul jealous of David?
options: Saul his thousands, David tens of thousands
explanation: Saul was angry that David got more praise. “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.” (1 Samuel 18:7, BSB)

content: In his jealousy, what did King Saul throw at David?
explanation: David escaped that night. “Saul tried to pin him to the wall with his spear.” (1 Samuel 19:10, BSB)

content: To send David a secret warning, what did Jonathan plan to shoot?
explanation: Where the arrows landed would tell David what to do. “I will shoot three arrows to the side of it” (1 Samuel 20:20, BSB)

content: When David and Jonathan said goodbye, what did they do?
explanation: David had to flee from Saul. “Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together” (1 Samuel 20:41, BSB)

content: When King Saul hunted David with three thousand men, where was David?
explanation: Saul was told where David was hiding. “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.” (1 Samuel 24:1, BSB)

content: When Saul stepped into a cave at En-gedi, who was hiding deep inside?
explanation: Saul did not know they were there. “And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.” (1 Samuel 24:3, BSB)

content: In the cave at En-gedi, what did David secretly cut off?
explanation: David could have killed Saul, but he did not. “Then David crept up secretly and cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.” (1 Samuel 24:4, BSB)

content: Why would David not harm King Saul in the cave?
explanation: David left Saul's fate to God. “May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.” (1 Samuel 24:6, BSB)

content: How did David feel after cutting the corner of Saul's robe?
explanation: Even that small act felt wrong to him. “Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken” (1 Samuel 24:5, BSB)

content: After David spared his life, what did King Saul say to him?
options: You are more righteous than I
explanation: David had repaid evil with good. “You are more righteous than I” (1 Samuel 24:17, BSB)

content: When Saul heard David calling to him outside the cave, what did Saul do?
explanation: Saul was moved by David's mercy. “Then Saul wept aloud” (1 Samuel 24:16, BSB)

content: Who were the two wives of Elkanah, Samuel's father?
explanation: Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none. “He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah.” (1 Samuel 1:2, BSB)

content: What did Hannah promise God if He gave her a son?
options: To give a lamb every year
To dedicate him to the LORD
explanation: She kept her promise. “then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life” (1 Samuel 1:11, BSB)

content: Why did Hannah name her son Samuel?
options: He was born in the temple
She asked the LORD for him
explanation: God answered her prayer. “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.” (1 Samuel 1:20, BSB)

content: When Samuel was a boy, how often did the word of the LORD come?
explanation: Visions were scarce in those days. “Now in those days the word of the LORD was rare and visions were scarce.” (1 Samuel 3:1, BSB)

content: When the Philistines captured the ark of God, which of Eli's sons died?
explanation: It was a dark day for Israel. “The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.” (1 Samuel 4:11, BSB)

content: When Samuel was old, what did the people of Israel ask him to give them?
explanation: They wanted to be like other nations. “Now appoint a king to judge us like all the other nations.” (1 Samuel 8:5, BSB)

content: When Israel asked Samuel for a king, whom did God say they had really rejected?
explanation: God was meant to be their king. “For it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected Me as their king.” (1 Samuel 8:7, BSB)

content: How is Saul described before he became Israel's first king?
explanation: He was choice and handsome. “a head taller than any of the people.” (1 Samuel 9:2, BSB)

content: When Samuel presented Saul to Israel as king, what did the people shout?
explanation: Saul became Israel's first king. “And all the people shouted, “Long live the king!”” (1 Samuel 10:24, BSB)

content: When Saul disobeyed, Samuel said the LORD had found a man after what?
explanation: That man would be David. “the LORD has sought a man after His own heart” (1 Samuel 13:14, BSB)

content: Samuel told disobedient King Saul that what is better than sacrifice?
explanation: God wants His people to listen and obey. “Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice” (1 Samuel 15:22, BSB)

content: Which of Jesse's sons did Samuel first think was God's chosen king?
explanation: Samuel judged by appearance at first. “When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab” (1 Samuel 16:6, BSB)

content: How is young David described when he was brought in from the sheep?
explanation: The LORD said, “He is the one.” “He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance.” (1 Samuel 16:12, BSB)

content: Goliath the giant came from which Philistine city?
explanation: He was the Philistines' champion. “Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath” (1 Samuel 17:4, BSB)

content: Before the battle with Goliath, what did David go back and forth to do?
explanation: He was still a shepherd in Bethlehem. “but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.” (1 Samuel 17:15, BSB)

content: Why did Saul first say David could not fight Goliath?
explanation: Goliath had been a warrior from his youth. “You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.” (1 Samuel 17:33, BSB)

content: David told Goliath that God does not save by sword or spear, because the battle belongs to whom?
explanation: David trusted God to win. “for the battle is the LORD’s” (1 Samuel 17:47, BSB)

content: After Goliath fell, what did the Philistine army do?
explanation: Their hero was dead. “When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran.” (1 Samuel 17:51, BSB)

content: Which of King Saul's daughters did David marry?
explanation: Saul gave her to David as his wife. “Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage.” (1 Samuel 18:27, BSB)

content: After the women's song about David, how did King Saul treat him?
options: Kept a jealous eye on him
explanation: Saul feared David would take the kingdom. “And from that day forward Saul kept a jealous eye on David.” (1 Samuel 18:9, BSB)

content: While running from Saul, where did David take refuge after leaving Gath?
explanation: His family came to him there. “So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam.” (1 Samuel 22:1, BSB)

content: Who was the wise wife of harsh Nabal?
explanation: She was intelligent and beautiful. “His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail.” (1 Samuel 25:3, BSB)

content: Before his last battle, whom did King Saul seek out at Endor?
explanation: Saul had turned away from the LORD. “There is a medium at Endor” (1 Samuel 28:7, BSB)

content: How did King Saul die in battle with the Philistines?
options: He fell on his own sword
explanation: His armor-bearer was too afraid to kill him. “So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.” (1 Samuel 31:4, BSB)

content: Elkanah, Samuel's father, came from which town?
explanation: It was in the hill country of Ephraim. “Now there was a man named Elkanah who was from Ramathaim-zophim” (1 Samuel 1:1, BSB)

content: Hannah promised that her son would never have what come over his head?
explanation: He would be set apart for God all his life. “and no razor shall ever come over his head.” (1 Samuel 1:11, BSB)

content: When God called young Samuel, what was wrong with old Eli?
explanation: Eli could not see. “Eli, whose eyesight had grown so dim that he could not see” (1 Samuel 3:2, BSB)

content: Samuel was known as a true prophet across Israel from where to where?
explanation: This meant the whole land. “So all Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew” (1 Samuel 3:20, BSB)

content: Which son of Jesse was presented to Samuel right after Abinadab?
explanation: The LORD had not chosen him either. “Next Jesse presented Shammah” (1 Samuel 16:9, BSB)

content: How tall was Goliath?
explanation: That is about nine and a half feet. “He was six cubits and a span in height” (1 Samuel 17:4, BSB)

content: How much did the iron point of Goliath's spear weigh?
explanation: His spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. “and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels.” (1 Samuel 17:7, BSB)

content: What was Goliath's coat of mail made of?
explanation: It weighed five thousand shekels. “He wore a bronze coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels” (1 Samuel 17:5, BSB)

content: How many Philistines did David and his men kill to become Saul's son-in-law?
explanation: Then Saul gave him Michal. “David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines.” (1 Samuel 18:27, BSB)

content: In Jonathan's arrow signal, which words meant David had to flee?
options: The arrows are on this side
explanation: It meant the LORD was sending David away. “Look, the arrows are beyond you” (1 Samuel 20:22, BSB)

content: How many chosen men did Saul take to hunt David near En-gedi?
explanation: They searched the rocky hills. “So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel” (1 Samuel 24:2, BSB)

content: In which rocky region did Saul look for David near En-gedi?
options: The Rocks of the Wild Goats
explanation: David was hiding in the caves there. “in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.” (1 Samuel 24:2, BSB)

content: Nabal, Abigail's harsh husband, belonged to which clan?
explanation: He was evil in his dealings. “but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.” (1 Samuel 25:3, BSB)

content: What did King Nebuchadnezzar set up on the plain of Dura for everyone to worship?
explanation: Everyone was ordered to bow down to it. “King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue” (Daniel 3:1, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: What would happen to anyone who did not bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
options: Be thrown into a fiery furnace
explanation: The king wanted everyone to obey. “will immediately be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.” (Daniel 3:6, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: Which three young Jews refused to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
explanation: They would worship only the true God. “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—who have ignored you, O king” (Daniel 3:12, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: Facing the furnace, what did Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego say their God was able to do?
explanation: They trusted God's power. “then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace” (Daniel 3:17, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego said that even if God did not save them, they would still never do what?
explanation: They would stay faithful no matter what. “we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.” (Daniel 3:18, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: How much hotter did Nebuchadnezzar order the furnace for the three friends?
explanation: The king was filled with rage. “He gave orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than usual” (Daniel 3:19, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: Looking into the fiery furnace, how many men did King Nebuchadnezzar see walking in the fire?
explanation: Someone was with them in the fire. “I see four men, unbound and unharmed, walking around in the fire” (Daniel 3:25, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: When the three friends came out of the fiery furnace, what was there no smell of on them?
explanation: Not even a hair was singed. “and there was no smell of fire on them.” (Daniel 3:27, BSB)
tags: Three Men in the Fiery Furnace

content: What law did King Darius's officials trick him into making to trap Daniel?
options: Pray to no one but the king
explanation: They knew Daniel prayed to God. “that for thirty days anyone who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.” (Daniel 6:7, BSB)

content: How long was King Darius's law against praying to anyone but him supposed to last?
explanation: Anyone who broke it would face the lions. “for thirty days” (Daniel 6:7, BSB)

content: After the law against prayer was signed, how many times a day did Daniel keep praying?
explanation: He prayed just as he had done before. “and three times a day he got down on his knees, prayed” (Daniel 6:10, BSB)

content: Which way did Daniel's windows face when he prayed in Babylon?
explanation: Jerusalem was the city of God's temple. “where the windows of his upper room opened toward Jerusalem” (Daniel 6:10, BSB)

content: Where was Daniel thrown for praying to God?
explanation: King Darius could not change the law. “and threw him into the den of lions.” (Daniel 6:16, BSB)

content: When did King Darius hurry to the lions' den to check on Daniel?
options: At the first light of dawn
explanation: The king could not wait to know. “At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the den of lions.” (Daniel 6:19, BSB)

content: How did God protect Daniel in the lions' den?
options: His angel shut the lions' mouths
explanation: Daniel was innocent before God. “My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions.” (Daniel 6:22, BSB)

content: Why were no wounds found on Daniel when he came out of the lions' den?
options: He had trusted in his God
explanation: Faith in God kept him safe. “because he had trusted in his God.” (Daniel 6:23, BSB)

content: As a young captive in Babylon, what did Daniel refuse to eat and drink?
explanation: He did not want to defile himself. “he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine.” (Daniel 1:8, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what did Daniel and his friends ask to eat for ten days?
explanation: They asked to be tested. “Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.” (Daniel 1:12, BSB)

content: After ten days of vegetables and water, how did Daniel and his friends look?
explanation: God blessed their choice. “they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men” (Daniel 1:15, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel given?
explanation: The chief official renamed all four young men. “To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar” (Daniel 1:7, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel's friend Hananiah given?
explanation: He later faced the fiery furnace. “to Hananiah, Shadrach” (Daniel 1:7, BSB)

content: Besides knowledge, what special gift did God give Daniel in Babylon?
explanation: This gift later helped him explain the king's dreams. “And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.” (Daniel 1:17, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream that Daniel explained, what was the statue's head made of?
explanation: Each metal stood for a kingdom. “The head of the statue was pure gold” (Daniel 2:32, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream that Daniel explained, what were the statue's feet made of?
explanation: The feet were the weak point. “and its feet were part iron and part clay.” (Daniel 2:33, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what did the stone that struck the statue become?
explanation: It filled the whole earth, like God's kingdom. “But the stone that had struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.” (Daniel 2:35, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, how was the stone that crushed the statue cut out?
explanation: It came from God, not people. “a stone was cut out, but not by human hands.” (Daniel 2:34, BSB)

content: What signal told everyone in Babylon to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
explanation: Horns, flutes, harps, and more were played. “As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music” (Daniel 3:5, BSB)

content: King Nebuchadnezzar said the fourth man in the fiery furnace looked like what?
explanation: God was with His servants in the fire. “and the fourth looks like a son of the gods!” (Daniel 3:25, BSB)

content: At King Belshazzar's feast, what appeared and wrote on the palace wall?
options: The fingers of a human hand
explanation: The king watched the hand writing. “At that moment the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall” (Daniel 5:5, BSB)

content: What words were written on the wall at King Belshazzar's feast?
explanation: Daniel explained what they meant. “MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.” (Daniel 5:25, BSB)

content: When jealous officials looked for a charge against Daniel, what did they find?
explanation: Daniel was trustworthy. “but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy” (Daniel 6:4, BSB)

content: Why did King Darius plan to set Daniel over the whole kingdom?
explanation: Daniel stood out among all the officials. “Soon, by his extraordinary spirit, Daniel distinguished himself among the administrators and satraps.” (Daniel 6:3, BSB)

content: As Daniel was thrown to the lions, what did King Darius say to him?
explanation: The king hoped Daniel's God would save him. “May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!” (Daniel 6:16, BSB)

content: During the reigns of which two kings did Daniel prosper?
explanation: God blessed Daniel's faithfulness. “So Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.” (Daniel 6:28, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel's friend Mishael given?
explanation: The chief official renamed him. “to Mishael, Meshach” (Daniel 1:7, BSB)

content: In Babylon, what new name was Daniel's friend Azariah given?
explanation: He was one of the three in the furnace. “and to Azariah, Abednego.” (Daniel 1:7, BSB)

content: On which plain did Nebuchadnezzar set up his golden statue?
explanation: It was in the province of Babylon. “and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.” (Daniel 3:1, BSB)

content: How high was Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
explanation: It was six cubits wide. “a golden statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide” (Daniel 3:1, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what were the statue's chest and arms made of?
explanation: The head was gold, the chest silver. “its chest and arms were silver” (Daniel 2:32, BSB)

content: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what were the statue's belly and thighs made of?
explanation: The legs were iron. “its belly and thighs were bronze” (Daniel 2:32, BSB)

content: At Belshazzar's feast, near what in the palace did the hand write on the wall?
explanation: The king could see it clearly. “near the lampstand in the royal palace.” (Daniel 5:5, BSB)

content: For how many days did Daniel ask to be tested on vegetables and water?
explanation: At the end they looked healthier than the rest. “Please test your servants for ten days.” (Daniel 1:12, BSB)

content: Before going to the king uninvited, what did Queen Esther ask the Jews in Susa to do?
explanation: She needed God's help. “Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa, and fast for me.” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: How many days did Queen Esther ask the Jews to fast before she went to the king?
explanation: Esther and her maidens fasted too. “Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: Knowing it was against the law to see the king uninvited, what did Esther say?
options: The king will never see me
explanation: Esther was willing to risk her life for her people. “And if I perish, I perish!” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: Mordecai told Esther that perhaps she had become queen for what?
explanation: God had placed her where she could help. “And who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” (Esther 4:14, BSB)

content: When Queen Esther came to the king uninvited, what did he hold out to her?
explanation: It meant she was welcome and would live. “The king extended the gold scepter in his hand toward Esther” (Esther 5:2, BSB)

content: When Esther came before the king, how much did he offer to give her?
explanation: She had found favor in his sight. “Even up to half the kingdom, it will be given to you.” (Esther 5:3, BSB)

content: On the night King Xerxes could not sleep, what did he have read to him?
explanation: There he learned that Mordecai had saved his life. “so he ordered the Book of Records, the Chronicles, to be brought in and read to him.” (Esther 6:1, BSB)

content: Whom did King Xerxes order Haman to honor with the royal robe and horse?
explanation: Haman had to honor the man he hated. “Take the robe and the horse to Mordecai the Jew” (Esther 6:10, BSB)

content: At her banquet, whom did Queen Esther name as the enemy of her people?
explanation: Haman stood in terror before the king and queen. “The adversary and enemy is this wicked man—Haman!” (Esther 7:6, BSB)

content: In the story of Queen Esther, what happened to Haman in the end?
options: He was hanged on his own gallows
explanation: The gallows he built for Mordecai was used for him. “So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.” (Esther 7:10, BSB)

content: In the book of Esther, which king reigned over 127 provinces?
explanation: He ruled a huge empire. “This is what happened in the days of Xerxes, who reigned over 127 provinces” (Esther 1:1, BSB)

content: Which queen refused to come when King Xerxes called her?
explanation: The king was furious with her. “Queen Vashti, however, refused to come at the king’s command” (Esther 1:12, BSB)

content: Who raised Esther after her parents died?
explanation: Mordecai took her in as his own daughter. “And Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther), the daughter of his uncle” (Esther 2:7, BSB)

content: What was Queen Esther's Hebrew name?
explanation: Esther was her Persian name. “Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther)” (Esther 2:7, BSB)

content: Why did King Xerxes make Esther his queen?
options: He loved her more than all others
She won a contest of strength
explanation: She found favor in his sight. “And the king loved Esther more than all the other women” (Esther 2:17, BSB)

content: When Mordecai learned of a plot to kill King Xerxes, whom did he tell?
explanation: Esther told the king on Mordecai's behalf. “he reported it to Queen Esther” (Esther 2:22, BSB)

content: In the book of Esther, why was Haman angry with Mordecai?
options: Mordecai would not bow to him
explanation: Everyone else at the king's gate bowed down. “But Mordecai would not bow down or pay homage.” (Esther 3:2, BSB)

content: Because of his anger at Mordecai, whom did Haman plan to destroy?
options: All the Jews in the kingdom
explanation: He hated Mordecai's whole people. “he sought to destroy all of Mordecai’s people, the Jews, throughout the kingdom of Xerxes.” (Esther 3:6, BSB)

content: What did Haman cast to choose the day to destroy the Jews?
explanation: The feast of Purim is named after it. “the Pur (that is, the lot) was cast before Haman” (Esther 3:7, BSB)

content: When Mordecai learned of Haman's plot against the Jews, what did he put on?
explanation: He mourned loudly in the city. “he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes” (Esther 4:1, BSB)

content: When King Xerxes learned Mordecai had saved his life, what reward had Mordecai been given?
explanation: So the king decided to honor him. ““Nothing has been done for him,” replied the king’s attendants.” (Esther 6:3, BSB)

content: After Haman's death, who received King Xerxes' signet ring?
explanation: Esther also put Mordecai over Haman's estate. “The king removed the signet ring he had recovered from Haman and presented it to Mordecai.” (Esther 8:2, BSB)

content: Which feast remembers how the Jews were saved in Queen Esther's day?
explanation: The name comes from the word Pur. “Therefore these days are called Purim, from the word Pur.” (Esther 9:26, BSB)

content: On the third day of fasting, where did Queen Esther stand in her royal robes?
options: The inner court of the palace
explanation: The king could see her from his throne. “Esther put on her royal attire and stood in the inner court of the palace” (Esther 5:1, BSB)

content: The kingdom of Xerxes in the book of Esther stretched from India to where?
explanation: It had 127 provinces. “who reigned over 127 provinces from India to Cush.” (Esther 1:1, BSB)

content: Which two eunuchs plotted to kill King Xerxes?
explanation: Mordecai uncovered their plot. “Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs who guarded the entrance” (Esther 2:21, BSB)

content: In the book of Esther, Haman was the son of Hammedatha and was called what?
explanation: King Xerxes raised him above all the princes. “Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite” (Esther 3:1, BSB)

content: In Haman's plot, in which month did the lot fall for destroying the Jews?
explanation: The lot was cast in the month of Nisan. “And the lot fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.” (Esther 3:7, BSB)

content: In which year of King Xerxes' reign was the Pur cast against the Jews?
explanation: It was cast in the first month. “In the twelfth year of King Xerxes” (Esther 3:7, BSB)

content: In which city did Queen Esther ask the Jews to gather and fast?
explanation: Susa was where the king's palace stood. “Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa” (Esther 4:16, BSB)

content: Esther told the king she would have stayed silent if her people had only been sold as what?
explanation: But they had been sold for destruction. “If we had merely been sold as menservants and maidservants, I would have remained silent” (Esther 7:4, BSB)

content: To save her baby boy from Pharaoh, what did Moses' mother put him in?
explanation: She coated it with tar and pitch so it would float. “she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch.” (Exodus 2:3, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: Where did Moses' mother place the basket with her baby inside?
options: Among the reeds by the Nile
explanation: She hid him along the riverbank. “set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.” (Exodus 2:3, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: Who stood at a distance to watch what would happen to baby Moses in the basket?
explanation: She kept watch over her little brother. “And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.” (Exodus 2:4, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: Who found baby Moses in his basket by the Nile?
explanation: She came down to the river to bathe. “Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile” (Exodus 2:5, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: Why did Pharaoh's daughter name the baby from the basket Moses?
options: He was born on the Nile
She drew him out of the water
explanation: Moses became her son. “She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”” (Exodus 2:10, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: While Moses was tending sheep at Horeb, what amazing sight did he see?
options: A burning bush not burning up
explanation: The angel of the LORD appeared in the fire. “Moses saw the bush ablaze with fire, but it was not consumed.” (Exodus 3:2, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: At the burning bush, what did God tell Moses to take off?
explanation: Moses was standing on holy ground. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.” (Exodus 3:5, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: At the burning bush, to whom did God send Moses?
explanation: Moses was to bring God's people out of Egypt. “I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.” (Exodus 3:10, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: When Moses asked God's name at the burning bush, what did God answer?
explanation: Moses was to tell Israel that I AM had sent him. “God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” (Exodus 3:14, BSB)
tags: Moses: The Basket and the Burning Bush

content: In the first plague on Egypt, what did the water of the Nile turn into?
explanation: Aaron struck the river with his staff. “and all the water was turned to blood.” (Exodus 7:20, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, God warned Pharaoh He would fill the country with which animal?
explanation: Pharaoh still refused to let the people go. “I will plague your whole country with frogs.” (Exodus 8:2, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, what fell from the sky with thunder and lightning?
explanation: Moses stretched his staff toward heaven. “So the LORD rained down hail upon the land of Egypt.” (Exodus 9:23, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, which insects did God bring after the hail?
explanation: They covered the land and ate what was left. “I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.” (Exodus 10:4, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, how long did total darkness cover the land?
explanation: No one in Egypt could see anyone else. “and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.” (Exodus 10:22, BSB)

content: Before the plagues began, what message from the LORD did Moses and Aaron bring Pharaoh?
explanation: God wanted His people to worship Him in the wilderness. “Let My people go” (Exodus 5:1, BSB)

content: When Moses first asked Pharaoh to free Israel, how did Pharaoh answer?
options: I will not let Israel go
explanation: Pharaoh said he did not know the LORD. “and I will not let Israel go.” (Exodus 5:2, BSB)

content: In front of Pharaoh, what did Aaron's staff do to the magicians' staffs?
explanation: God showed He was greater than Egypt's magic. “But Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs.” (Exodus 7:12, BSB)

content: For the first Passover, what animal was each family to choose?
explanation: One lamb was chosen for each household. “each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household.” (Exodus 12:3, BSB)

content: For the first Passover, what kind of lamb was needed?
explanation: The lamb had to be perfect. “Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male” (Exodus 12:5, BSB)

content: At the first Passover, where did the Israelites put the lamb's blood?
explanation: The blood marked the houses of God's people. “They are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes” (Exodus 12:7, BSB)

content: At the first Passover, what did the Israelites eat with the roasted lamb?
explanation: They ate the meal that same night. “along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.” (Exodus 12:8, BSB)

content: At the first Passover, what did God do when He saw the blood on a house?
explanation: That is why the feast is called the Passover. “when I see the blood, I will pass over you.” (Exodus 12:13, BSB)

content: At midnight on the first Passover, what happened in Egypt?
explanation: It was the last of the ten plagues. “Now at midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn male in the land of Egypt” (Exodus 12:29, BSB)

content: After the tenth plague, what did Pharaoh tell Moses and the Israelites?
explanation: Pharaoh finally let God's people go. “Get up, leave my people, both you and the Israelites!” (Exodus 12:31, BSB)

content: As the Israelites left Egypt, what went before them to guide them by day?
explanation: By night a pillar of fire gave them light. “And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day” (Exodus 13:21, BSB)

content: When Pharaoh's army chased Israel to the edge of the sea, how did the Israelites feel?
explanation: They cried out to the LORD. “and they were terrified and cried out to the LORD.” (Exodus 14:10, BSB)

content: At the sea, Moses said the LORD would fight for Israel. What did the people need to do?
explanation: God Himself would save them. “The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still.” (Exodus 14:14, BSB)

content: At the sea, what did God tell Moses to lift up and stretch out over the water?
explanation: God would divide the sea. “lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it” (Exodus 14:16, BSB)

content: When Israel was trapped by the sea, what did the LORD use to drive back the water all night?
explanation: The wind turned the sea into dry land. “the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land.” (Exodus 14:21, BSB)

content: When God divided the sea, how did the Israelites cross?
explanation: Walls of water stood on both sides. “and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground” (Exodus 14:22, BSB)

content: What happened to Pharaoh's army when it followed Israel into the sea?
explanation: Not one of them survived. “The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen” (Exodus 14:28, BSB)

content: After Israel crossed the sea, who led the women with tambourines and dancing?
explanation: Miriam was Aaron's sister and a prophetess. “Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a tambourine in her hand” (Exodus 15:20, BSB)

content: In the wilderness after leaving Egypt, what did the hungry Israelites complain about?
explanation: They remembered the food of Egypt. “but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!” (Exodus 16:3, BSB)

content: When Israel was hungry in the wilderness, what did God promise to rain down from heaven?
explanation: The people were to gather enough each day. “Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you.” (Exodus 16:4, BSB)

content: That evening in the wilderness, what birds came and covered Israel's camp?
explanation: God gave them meat in the evening. “That evening quail came and covered the camp” (Exodus 16:13, BSB)

content: When the Israelites first saw thin flakes on the desert floor, what did they ask?
explanation: Moses told them it was bread from the LORD. “they asked one another, “What is it?”” (Exodus 16:15, BSB)

content: What did the Israelites call the bread God gave them in the wilderness?
explanation: They ate it every day in the wilderness. “Now the house of Israel called the bread manna.” (Exodus 16:31, BSB)

content: What did the manna in the wilderness taste like?
explanation: God's bread was sweet. “and tasted like wafers made with honey.” (Exodus 16:31, BSB)

content: For how many years did the Israelites eat manna?
explanation: They ate it until they reached Canaan. “The Israelites ate manna forty years” (Exodus 16:35, BSB)

content: Which commandment comes first in the Ten Commandments?
explanation: God comes first. “You shall have no other gods before Me.” (Exodus 20:3, BSB)

content: In the Ten Commandments, which day were God's people told to keep holy?
explanation: It was a day of rest for the LORD. “Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.” (Exodus 20:8, BSB)

content: Which of the Ten Commandments comes with a promise of long life in the land?
explanation: God promised long days to those who honor their parents. “Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land” (Exodus 20:12, BSB)

content: Which of the Ten Commandments says not to take what belongs to others?
explanation: God's people respect what belongs to others. “You shall not steal.” (Exodus 20:15, BSB)

content: In the Ten Commandments, what must you not bear against your neighbor?
explanation: God's people must not lie about others. “You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.” (Exodus 20:16, BSB)

content: When God came down to give His law, what covered Mount Sinai?
explanation: The LORD came down on the mountain in fire. “Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke” (Exodus 19:18, BSB)

content: What were the tablets God gave Moses on Mount Sinai made of?
explanation: They held the words of God's covenant. “tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God.” (Exodus 31:18, BSB)

content: Who wrote on the stone tablets God gave Moses?
explanation: God Himself wrote His law. “inscribed by the finger of God.” (Exodus 31:18, BSB)

content: While Moses stayed long on Mount Sinai, what did the people ask Aaron to make?
explanation: They grew tired of waiting for Moses. “Come, make us gods who will go before us.” (Exodus 32:1, BSB)

content: At Mount Sinai, what did Aaron tell the people to bring him to make an idol?
explanation: He melted the gold to make the idol. “Take off the gold earrings” (Exodus 32:2, BSB)

content: What did Aaron make from the people's gold at Mount Sinai?
explanation: The people said the calf had brought them out of Egypt. “he fashioned it into a molten calf.” (Exodus 32:4, BSB)

content: When Moses came down and saw the golden calf, what did he do with the stone tablets?
explanation: Moses burned with anger at the people's sin. “he burned with anger and threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them” (Exodus 32:19, BSB)

content: What did Moses do to the golden calf?
options: Burned it and ground it to powder
explanation: He destroyed the idol completely. “burned it in the fire, ground it to powder” (Exodus 32:20, BSB)

content: After the golden calf, Moses said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.” Who came?
explanation: The Levites stood with the LORD. “And all the Levites gathered around him.” (Exodus 32:26, BSB)

content: Why did the people at Mount Sinai ask Aaron to make them gods?
options: Moses was delayed on the mountain
explanation: They did not know what had happened to Moses. “Now when the people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain” (Exodus 32:1, BSB)

content: At the start of Exodus, what was different about the new king who came to power in Egypt?
explanation: He feared the Israelites and made them slaves. “Then a new king, who did not know Joseph, came to power in Egypt.” (Exodus 1:8, BSB)

content: Which store cities did the enslaved Israelites build for Pharaoh?
explanation: Taskmasters forced them into hard labor. “they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.” (Exodus 1:11, BSB)

content: Why did the Hebrew midwives refuse Pharaoh's order to kill the baby boys?
explanation: They let the boys live. “The midwives, however, feared God” (Exodus 1:17, BSB)

content: Whom did Pharaoh's daughter pay to nurse baby Moses?
explanation: Moses' sister cleverly brought their mother. “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” (Exodus 2:9, BSB)

content: After Moses killed an Egyptian, where did he flee to escape Pharaoh?
explanation: There he sat down beside a well. “But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian” (Exodus 2:15, BSB)

content: In Midian, whom did Moses marry?
explanation: She was the daughter of the priest of Midian. “and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.” (Exodus 2:21, BSB)

content: Whose flock was Moses tending when he saw the burning bush?
explanation: Jethro was the priest of Midian. “Moses was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Jethro” (Exodus 3:1, BSB)

content: At the burning bush, how did God describe the land He would give Israel?
explanation: It was a good and spacious land. “a land flowing with milk and honey” (Exodus 3:8, BSB)

content: At the burning bush, what did Moses' staff become when he threw it down?
explanation: It was a sign so the people would believe Moses. “and it became a snake, and he ran from it.” (Exodus 4:3, BSB)

content: At the burning bush, why did Moses say he could not speak to Pharaoh?
explanation: God promised to teach him what to say. “for I am slow of speech and tongue.” (Exodus 4:10, BSB)

content: When Moses asked God to send someone else, whom did God send to speak for him?
explanation: Aaron could speak well. “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well” (Exodus 4:14, BSB)

content: After Moses first spoke to Pharaoh, what did Pharaoh stop giving the Hebrew slaves?
explanation: Pharaoh made their work even harder. “You shall no longer supply the people with straw for making bricks.” (Exodus 5:7, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, what did the dust turn into when Aaron struck it?
explanation: Swarms of gnats covered the land. “that it may turn into swarms of gnats throughout the land of Egypt.” (Exodus 8:16, BSB)

content: During the plagues on Egypt, what broke out on people and animals from fine dust?
explanation: Even the magicians were struck with boils. “and festering boils will break out on man and beast” (Exodus 9:9, BSB)

content: What was the tenth and final plague on Egypt?
explanation: After it, Pharaoh let Israel go. “and every firstborn son in the land of Egypt will die” (Exodus 11:5, BSB)

content: After crossing the sea, why could the Israelites not drink the water at Marah?
explanation: Marah means bitter. “they could not drink the water there because it was bitter.” (Exodus 15:23, BSB)

content: At Marah, what did Moses throw into the bitter water to make it sweet?
explanation: The LORD showed him the log. “And when he cast it into the waters, they were sweetened.” (Exodus 15:25, BSB)

content: When Israel had no water at Horeb, what did God tell Moses to strike?
explanation: Water came out for the people to drink. “And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.” (Exodus 17:6, BSB)

content: In Israel's battle with Amalek, when did Israel win?
options: When Moses held up his hands
explanation: When Moses lowered his hands, Amalek won. “As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed” (Exodus 17:11, BSB)

content: In the battle with Amalek, who held up Moses' tired hands?
explanation: They held his hands steady until sunset. “Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side” (Exodus 17:12, BSB)

content: When Moses was worn out judging the people, what did Jethro advise him to do?
explanation: The work was too heavy for one man. “Appoint them over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.” (Exodus 18:21, BSB)

content: The Ten Commandments forbid making an idol in the form of what?
options: Anything in heaven, earth, or water
explanation: Nothing created should be worshiped. “You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.” (Exodus 20:4, BSB)

content: What reason do the Ten Commandments give for resting on the Sabbath?
options: God rested on the seventh day
explanation: God made everything in six days. “but on the seventh day He rested.” (Exodus 20:11, BSB)

content: How long did Moses stay on Mount Sinai inside the cloud?
explanation: God gave him instructions there. “and he remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.” (Exodus 24:18, BSB)

content: How did the LORD speak with Moses at the tent of meeting?
options: Face to face, like a friend
explanation: Moses had a close friendship with God. “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11, BSB)

content: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the new tablets, what was different about him?
explanation: He had been speaking with the LORD. “he was unaware that his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD.” (Exodus 34:29, BSB)

content: When the tabernacle was finished, what filled it?
explanation: The cloud covered the Tent of Meeting. “and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.” (Exodus 40:34, BSB)

content: What were the names of the Hebrew midwives who disobeyed Pharaoh?
explanation: They feared God more than the king. “whose names were Shiphrah and Puah” (Exodus 1:15, BSB)

content: How long did Moses' mother hide him before putting him in a basket?
explanation: She saw he was a beautiful child. “she hid him for three months.” (Exodus 2:2, BSB)

content: What did Moses name the son Zipporah bore him in Midian?
explanation: Moses felt like a foreigner in a foreign land. “and Moses named him Gershom” (Exodus 2:22, BSB)

content: At which mountain did Moses see the burning bush?
explanation: He had led the flock to the far side of the wilderness. “and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.” (Exodus 3:1, BSB)

content: About how many men on foot left Egypt with Moses?
explanation: Women and children came too. “with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.” (Exodus 12:37, BSB)

content: How long had the Israelites lived in Egypt before the exodus?
explanation: Then they left on the very same day. “Now the duration of the Israelites’ stay in Egypt was 430 years.” (Exodus 12:40, BSB)

content: From which city did the Israelites set out when they left Egypt?
explanation: Their first stop was Succoth. “The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth” (Exodus 12:37, BSB)

content: Near which place did Pharaoh's army catch up with Israel camped by the sea?
explanation: It was opposite Baal-zephon. “as they camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon.” (Exodus 14:9, BSB)

content: What did the manna in the wilderness look like?
explanation: It tasted like honey wafers. “It was white like coriander seed” (Exodus 16:31, BSB)

content: What kind of wood was the ark of the covenant made of?
explanation: God gave exact measurements for the ark. “And they are to construct an ark of acacia wood” (Exodus 25:10, BSB)

content: Who was Moses' young assistant who would not leave the tent of meeting?
explanation: Joshua later led Israel into Canaan. “but his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.” (Exodus 33:11, BSB)

content: During Moses' second forty days on Mount Sinai, what did he go without?
explanation: He wrote the Ten Commandments on the tablets. “without eating bread or drinking water.” (Exodus 34:28, BSB)

content: The Ten Commandments say God shows loving devotion to how many generations of those who love Him?
explanation: His love lasts far longer than punishment. “but showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me” (Exodus 20:6, BSB)

content: In the very beginning, what did God create?
explanation: The Bible's first sentence tells us God made everything. “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.” (Genesis 1:1, BSB)

content: On the first day of creation, what did God make just by speaking?
explanation: God spoke, and light appeared. “And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.” (Genesis 1:3, BSB)

content: During creation, what name did God give the light?
explanation: God named the light and the darkness. “God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.”” (Genesis 1:5, BSB)

content: On the fourth day of creation, what else did God make besides the two great lights?
explanation: God filled the sky with lights to mark days and seasons. “And He made the stars as well.” (Genesis 1:16, BSB)

content: During creation, in whose image did God create people?
explanation: People are special because they reflect God. “So God created man in His own image” (Genesis 1:27, BSB)

content: At the end of the sixth day, how did God describe everything He had made?
explanation: God was pleased with all He had made. “and indeed, it was very good.” (Genesis 1:31, BSB)

content: After creating everything, what did God do on the seventh day?
explanation: God finished His work and rested. “so on that day He rested from all His work.” (Genesis 2:2, BSB)

content: In the creation story, what did God form the first man from?
explanation: Then God breathed the breath of life into him. “Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground” (Genesis 2:7, BSB)

content: In the creation story, what did God use to make the first woman?
explanation: God made a helper suitable for the man. “And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman” (Genesis 2:22, BSB)

content: In the Garden of Eden, which creature tricked the woman?
explanation: The serpent made her doubt what God had said. “Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field” (Genesis 3:1, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: In Eden, after the woman ate the forbidden fruit, who did she give some to?
explanation: Adam was with her, and he ate too. “She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.” (Genesis 3:6, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: After eating the forbidden fruit, what did Adam and Eve sew together to cover themselves?
explanation: Their eyes were opened and they felt ashamed. “so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.” (Genesis 3:7, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: When Adam and Eve heard God walking in the garden, what did they do?
explanation: Sin made them afraid to face God. “they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.” (Genesis 3:8, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: After Adam and Eve hid in the garden, what did God call out to Adam?
explanation: God came looking for them. “But the LORD God called out to the man, “Where are you?”” (Genesis 3:9, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: When God asked Eve what she had done, whom did she blame?
explanation: Adam blamed Eve, and Eve blamed the serpent. ““The serpent deceived me,” she replied, “and I ate.”” (Genesis 3:13, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: After the first sin, what name did Adam give his wife?
explanation: She would be the mother of all the living. “And Adam named his wife Eve” (Genesis 3:20, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: After sending Adam and Eve out of Eden, what did God place to guard the tree of life?
explanation: The way back to the tree of life was closed. “and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame” (Genesis 3:24, BSB)
tags: The Garden of Eden and the First Sin

content: What job did Abel, Adam's son, have?
explanation: Abel was a shepherd; his brother Cain was a farmer. “Now Abel was a keeper of sheep” (Genesis 4:2, BSB)

content: What job did Cain, Adam's son, have?
explanation: Cain was a farmer; his brother Abel was a shepherd. “while Cain was a tiller of the soil.” (Genesis 4:2, BSB)

content: When Cain and Abel brought offerings, whose offering did God look on with favor?
explanation: Abel brought the best of his flock. “And the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering” (Genesis 4:4, BSB)

content: How did Cain feel when God did not accept his offering?
explanation: His anger led him to sin. “So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.” (Genesis 4:5, BSB)

content: Out in the field, what did Cain do to his brother Abel?
explanation: This was the first murder in the Bible. “Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.” (Genesis 4:8, BSB)

content: When God asked Cain where Abel was, what did Cain answer?
explanation: Cain tried to hide what he had done. ““Am I my brother’s keeper?”” (Genesis 4:9, BSB)

content: After Cain killed Abel, what did God put on Cain to protect him?
explanation: The mark kept others from killing Cain. “And the LORD placed a mark on Cain” (Genesis 4:15, BSB)

content: When the world was full of evil, who found favor in the eyes of the LORD?
explanation: Noah walked with God in a wicked world. “Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.” (Genesis 6:8, BSB)

content: Before the flood, how many sons did Noah have?
explanation: His sons were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. “And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” (Genesis 6:10, BSB)

content: Before the flood, what did God tell Noah to build?
explanation: The ark would keep Noah's family and the animals alive. “Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood” (Genesis 6:14, BSB)

content: What kind of animal pairs did God tell Noah to bring into the ark?
explanation: The animals would fill the earth again after the flood. “you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark—male and female” (Genesis 6:19, BSB)

content: In Noah's flood, how long did the rain fall?
explanation: The waters covered even the high mountains. “And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.” (Genesis 7:12, BSB)

content: When the floodwaters went down, where did Noah's ark come to rest?
explanation: The ark settled as the waters slowly went down. “the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.” (Genesis 8:4, BSB)

content: After the flood, what was the first bird Noah sent out of the ark?
explanation: Later Noah sent out a dove. “and sent out a raven.” (Genesis 8:7, BSB)

content: After the flood, what did the dove bring back to Noah in her beak?
explanation: Noah knew the waters had gone down. “the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak.” (Genesis 8:11, BSB)

content: When Noah came out of the ark, what did he build?
explanation: Noah thanked God with burnt offerings. “Then Noah built an altar to the LORD.” (Genesis 8:20, BSB)

content: After the flood, what sign of His promise did God set in the clouds?
explanation: God promised never again to destroy the earth by a flood. “I have set My rainbow in the clouds” (Genesis 9:13, BSB)

content: Before the Tower of Babel, how many languages did the whole world speak?
explanation: Everyone could understand everyone else. “Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech.” (Genesis 11:1, BSB)

content: When people built the Tower of Babel, what did they use instead of stone?
explanation: They baked bricks to build their city and tower. “So they used brick instead of stone” (Genesis 11:3, BSB)

content: Why did the people at Babel want a tower that reached to the heavens?
options: To make a name for themselves
explanation: They wanted fame and to stay together in one place. “that we may make a name for ourselves” (Genesis 11:4, BSB)

content: At the Tower of Babel, what did God do to the people's language?
explanation: They could no longer understand one another. “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language” (Genesis 11:7, BSB)

content: After God confused their language, what did the builders at Babel stop doing?
explanation: God scattered them over all the earth. “and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8, BSB)

content: What was the city with the unfinished tower called?
explanation: There the LORD confused the language of the whole world. “That is why it is called Babel” (Genesis 11:9, BSB)

content: In the Garden of Eden, which two trees stood in the middle of the garden?
options: A fig tree and a vine
Tree of life, tree of knowledge
explanation: God told Adam not to eat from the tree of knowledge. “And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.” (Genesis 2:9, BSB)

content: Why did God put the first man in the Garden of Eden?
explanation: From the start, God gave people good work to do. “and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.” (Genesis 2:15, BSB)

content: In the Garden of Eden, what did God say was not good?
options: For the garden to be empty
For the man to be alone
For the animals to be wild
explanation: So God made a suitable helper for him. “It is not good for the man to be alone.” (Genesis 2:18, BSB)

content: In the Garden of Eden, who gave names to all the animals?
explanation: God brought the animals to the man to name them. “The man gave names to all the livestock” (Genesis 2:20, BSB)

content: After the first sin, God told the serpent the woman's offspring would crush what?
explanation: This is the first promise that evil would be defeated. “He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.” (Genesis 3:15, BSB)

content: After the first sin, God told Adam he would one day return to what?
explanation: Adam was made from the ground. “For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.” (Genesis 3:19, BSB)

content: After the first sin, what did God make to clothe Adam and Eve?
explanation: God cared for them even after they sinned. “And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.” (Genesis 3:21, BSB)

content: When Cain was angry, God warned him that something was crouching at his door. What?
explanation: God told Cain he must master it. “sin is crouching at your door” (Genesis 4:7, BSB)

content: After killing Abel, where did Cain go to live?
explanation: Nod was east of Eden. “and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.” (Genesis 4:16, BSB)

content: After Abel died, what did Adam and Eve name their next son?
explanation: Eve said God had given her another child in place of Abel. “she gave birth to a son and named him Seth” (Genesis 4:25, BSB)

content: In the family line from Adam to Noah, who lived a total of 969 years?
explanation: He is the oldest person named in the Bible. “So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years” (Genesis 5:27, BSB)

content: Before the flood, which man walked with God and then was taken away by God?
explanation: Enoch did not die like the others in his family line. “Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.” (Genesis 5:24, BSB)

content: What kind of wood did God tell Noah to use for the ark?
explanation: God gave Noah exact building instructions. “Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood” (Genesis 6:14, BSB)

content: How does Genesis describe Noah's character before the flood?
explanation: Noah walked with God. “Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation” (Genesis 6:9, BSB)

content: After the flood, God promised that as long as the earth lasts, what would never stop?
options: Seedtime and harvest, day and night
explanation: God promised a steady world after the flood. “seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.” (Genesis 8:22, BSB)

content: How long did God tell Noah to make the ark?
explanation: It was also 50 cubits wide and 30 cubits high. “The ark is to be 300 cubits long” (Genesis 6:15, BSB)

content: In Noah's flood, how long did the waters prevail on the earth?
explanation: The rain lasted forty days, but the water stayed much longer. “And the waters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days.” (Genesis 7:24, BSB)

content: How many pairs of each kind of clean animal did Noah take into the ark?
explanation: Unclean animals came in one pair each. “You are to take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal” (Genesis 7:2, BSB)

content: How old was Noah when the floodwaters burst forth?
explanation: It happened on the seventeenth day of the second month. “In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life” (Genesis 7:11, BSB)

content: Where did people settle before building the Tower of Babel?
options: A plain in the land of Shinar
explanation: They journeyed eastward and settled there. “they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.” (Genesis 11:2, BSB)

content: After whom did Cain name the city he built?
explanation: This Enoch is not the Enoch who walked with God. “Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.” (Genesis 4:17, BSB)

content: When building at Babel, what did people use instead of mortar?
explanation: They also used brick instead of stone. “and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3, BSB)

content: In the family line from Adam to Noah, how many years did Enoch live in all?
explanation: Then God took him away. “So Enoch lived a total of 365 years.” (Genesis 5:23, BSB)

content: When God called Abram, what did He tell him to leave behind?
explanation: God asked Abram to go to a land He would show him. “Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household” (Genesis 12:1, BSB)

content: When God called Abram, what did He promise to make him into?
explanation: God also promised to bless him. “I will make you into a great nation” (Genesis 12:2, BSB)

content: When Abram obeyed God's call and left Haran, which nephew went with him?
explanation: Abram took Sarai and Lot with him. “and Lot went with him.” (Genesis 12:4, BSB)

content: When Abram obeyed God's call, which land did he set out for?
explanation: This was the land God promised to his offspring. “and set out for the land of Canaan.” (Genesis 12:5, BSB)

content: When God appeared to Abram in Canaan, what did Abram build there?
explanation: Abram worshiped the God who had spoken to him. “So Abram built an altar there to the LORD” (Genesis 12:7, BSB)

content: When God called Abram, who did He say would be blessed through him?
options: All the families of the earth
explanation: God's plan for Abram reached the whole world. “and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.” (Genesis 12:3, BSB)

content: When God gave childless Abram a promise at night, what did He tell him to count?
explanation: Abram's offspring would be as many as the stars. “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” (Genesis 15:5, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: In a vision, God told Abram, “Do not be afraid. I am your…” what?
explanation: God promised to protect Abram and be his reward. “I am your shield, your very great reward.” (Genesis 15:1, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: When God promised Abram offspring like the stars, how did Abram respond?
explanation: God counted Abram's faith as righteousness. “Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.” (Genesis 15:6, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: Before God's promise of offspring like the stars, what was Abram worried about?
explanation: A servant was going to inherit everything. “since I remain childless” (Genesis 15:2, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: God promised childless Abram that his heir would be whom?
explanation: God promised Abram a child of his own. “but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.” (Genesis 15:4, BSB)
tags: The Promise: Offspring Like the Stars

content: When two angels came to Sodom in the evening, who was sitting in the city gateway?
explanation: Lot got up to meet them and bowed down. “and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city.” (Genesis 19:1, BSB)

content: At daybreak in Sodom, what did the angels urge Lot to do?
options: Fight the men of the city
explanation: The city was about to be destroyed. “Take your wife and your two daughters who are here” (Genesis 19:15, BSB)

content: As Lot's family fled Sodom, what did the angels tell them not to do?
explanation: They had to run for their lives to the mountains. “Do not look back” (Genesis 19:17, BSB)

content: What did the LORD rain down on Sodom and Gomorrah?
explanation: God judged the wicked cities. “Then the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah” (Genesis 19:24, BSB)

content: When Lot's wife looked back at Sodom, what did she become?
explanation: She did not obey the angels' warning. “But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.” (Genesis 19:26, BSB)

content: When Lot hesitated to leave Sodom, what did the angels do?
options: Took their hands and led them out
explanation: The LORD had compassion on Lot's family. “the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters.” (Genesis 19:16, BSB)

content: What did Abraham name the son that Sarah bore him in their old age?
explanation: God kept His promise to Abraham and Sarah. “And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.” (Genesis 21:3, BSB)

content: How old was Abraham when his son Isaac was born?
explanation: Nothing is too hard for the LORD. “Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.” (Genesis 21:5, BSB)

content: After Isaac was born, what did Sarah say God had made her do?
explanation: Her laugh of doubt became a laugh of joy. “God has made me laugh” (Genesis 21:6, BSB)

content: What did Abraham hold on the day his son Isaac was weaned?
explanation: The family celebrated the promised child. “and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.” (Genesis 21:8, BSB)

content: When Hagar and her boy ran out of water in the wilderness, what did God show her?
explanation: God heard the boy's voice and cared for them. “Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water.” (Genesis 21:19, BSB)

content: When was Isaac born to Abraham and Sarah?
options: At the very time God promised
explanation: God did exactly what He had said. “at the very time God had promised.” (Genesis 21:2, BSB)

content: When God tested Abraham, whom did He tell him to offer?
explanation: God was testing Abraham's trust. “your only son Isaac, whom you love” (Genesis 22:2, BSB)

content: When God tested Abraham, which land did He send him to?
explanation: God would show him one of the mountains there. “and go to the land of Moriah.” (Genesis 22:2, BSB)

content: As Abraham and Isaac walked up the mountain, what did Isaac carry?
explanation: Abraham carried the fire and the knife. “Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac.” (Genesis 22:6, BSB)

content: On the way up the mountain, what did Isaac ask his father Abraham?
explanation: Isaac saw the fire and wood but no lamb. “but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?” (Genesis 22:7, BSB)

content: When Isaac asked where the lamb was, what did Abraham answer?
explanation: Abraham trusted God to provide. “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” (Genesis 22:8, BSB)

content: Just as Abraham took the knife on the mountain, who called out to stop him?
explanation: Abraham had shown that he feared God. “Just then the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven” (Genesis 22:11, BSB)

content: On the mountain, what did Abraham offer in place of his son Isaac?
options: A ram caught in a thicket
explanation: God provided a ram, caught by its horns. “and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns.” (Genesis 22:13, BSB)

content: In his old age, Abraham sent his servant to find a wife for whom?
explanation: The wife was to come from Abraham's own relatives. “to take a wife for my son Isaac.” (Genesis 24:4, BSB)

content: What animals did Abraham's servant take on his trip to find a wife for Isaac?
explanation: He also took many good gifts from his master. “Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels” (Genesis 24:10, BSB)

content: Looking for a wife for Isaac, where did Abraham's servant stop his camels to pray?
options: By a well outside the town
explanation: It was the time women came to draw water. “he made the camels kneel down near the well outside the town” (Genesis 24:11, BSB)

content: While Abraham's servant was still praying at the well, who came out with her jar?
explanation: God answered before he finished praying. “Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder.” (Genesis 24:15, BSB)

content: At the well, what did Rebekah offer to do for the camels of Abraham's servant?
explanation: This was the sign the servant had prayed for. “I will also draw water for your camels, until they have had enough to drink.” (Genesis 24:19, BSB)

content: When her family asked Rebekah if she would go with Abraham's servant to marry Isaac, what did she say?
explanation: Rebekah chose to go to Isaac. ““I will go,” she replied.” (Genesis 24:58, BSB)

content: How did Isaac feel about Rebekah after he married her?
explanation: She comforted him after his mother's death. “And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.” (Genesis 24:67, BSB)

content: When Rebekah, Isaac's wife, gave birth, what was special about her children?
explanation: The twins were Esau and Jacob. “there were indeed twins in her womb.” (Genesis 25:24, BSB)

content: Which of Isaac's twins was born first, red and hairy?
explanation: He was covered with hair like a fur coat. “The first one came out red, covered with hair like a fur coat; so they named him Esau.” (Genesis 25:25, BSB)

content: When Jacob was born right after his twin, what was he holding on to?
explanation: That is how he got the name Jacob. “his brother came out grasping Esau’s heel” (Genesis 25:26, BSB)

content: When Isaac's twins grew up, what kind of man was Esau?
explanation: Jacob was the quiet one who stayed at home. “Esau became a skillful hunter” (Genesis 25:27, BSB)

content: One day Esau came in from the field very hungry. What was Jacob cooking?
explanation: Esau begged for some of the red stew. “while Jacob was cooking some stew” (Genesis 25:29, BSB)

content: What did Jacob ask Esau to sell him for a bowl of stew?
explanation: Esau traded something precious for one meal. ““First sell me your birthright,” Jacob replied.” (Genesis 25:31, BSB)

content: Which of the twin brothers did their mother Rebekah love?
explanation: Isaac loved Esau, but Rebekah loved Jacob. “but Rebekah loved Jacob.” (Genesis 25:28, BSB)

content: How old was Abram when he left Haran at God's call?
explanation: Abram obeyed God even in old age. “Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.” (Genesis 12:4, BSB)

content: When a severe famine struck Canaan, where did Abram go to live for a while?
explanation: There was not enough food in the land. “So Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.” (Genesis 12:10, BSB)

content: When Abram and Lot separated, which land did Lot choose for himself?
explanation: It looked well watered like the garden of the LORD. “So Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself” (Genesis 13:11, BSB)

content: After separating from Abram, Lot pitched his tent toward which city?
explanation: Lot moved near the wicked city of Sodom. “and pitched his tent toward Sodom.” (Genesis 13:12, BSB)

content: Which king of Salem brought bread and wine to Abram?
explanation: He was priest of God Most High. “Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine” (Genesis 14:18, BSB)

content: After Melchizedek blessed him, what did Abram give Melchizedek?
explanation: Abram honored the priest of God Most High. “Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.” (Genesis 14:20, BSB)

content: What was the name of Sarai's Egyptian maidservant?
explanation: Sarai gave Hagar to Abram because she had no children. “but she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.” (Genesis 16:1, BSB)

content: What did Abram name the son that Hagar bore him?
explanation: Ishmael was born before Isaac. “and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.” (Genesis 16:15, BSB)

content: When God made His covenant with Abram, what new name did He give him?
explanation: His new name meant he would be a father of many nations. “but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.” (Genesis 17:5, BSB)

content: When God renamed Abraham, what new name did He give Abraham's wife Sarai?
explanation: God promised she would be the mother of nations. “for her name is to be Sarah.” (Genesis 17:15, BSB)

content: When God appeared to Abram at age ninety-nine, what name did He call Himself?
explanation: God told Abram to walk before Him and be blameless. “I am God Almighty.” (Genesis 17:1, BSB)

content: By the Oaks of Mamre, how many men did Abraham see standing near his tent?
explanation: Abraham ran to welcome his visitors. “And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby.” (Genesis 18:2, BSB)

content: When Sarah overheard that she would have a son in her old age, what did she do?
explanation: She thought she was too old. “So she laughed to herself” (Genesis 18:12, BSB)

content: When Sarah laughed at the promise of a son, what did the LORD ask Abraham?
options: Is anything too difficult for the LORD?
explanation: God promised Sarah would have a son in about a year. “Is anything too difficult for the LORD?” (Genesis 18:14, BSB)

content: When Abraham pleaded for Sodom, what was the smallest number of righteous people he asked about?
explanation: God said He would spare the city for ten. “Suppose ten are found there?” (Genesis 18:32, BSB)

content: What did Abraham name the mountain where God provided a ram in Isaac's place?
explanation: God had provided the sacrifice. “And Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide.” (Genesis 22:14, BSB)

content: After Abraham's test on the mountain, God promised to multiply his descendants like what?
explanation: Abraham had not held back his only son. “I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore.” (Genesis 22:17, BSB)

content: What was the name of Rebekah's brother, who rushed out to meet Abraham's servant?
explanation: Bethuel was her father; Laban was her brother. “Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban” (Genesis 24:29, BSB)

content: What was Isaac doing in the field when Rebekah's camels came into view?
explanation: He looked up and saw the camels approaching. “Isaac went out to the field to meditate” (Genesis 24:63, BSB)

content: Because he asked for the red stew, what other name was Esau given?
explanation: Edom sounds like the word for red. “(That is why he was also called Edom.)” (Genesis 25:30, BSB)

content: What did Jacob give Esau in exchange for his birthright?
explanation: Esau ate, drank, and went away. “Then Jacob gave some bread and lentil stew to Esau” (Genesis 25:34, BSB)

content: Before Rebekah's twins were born, what did God say about the older and the younger?
options: The younger will serve the older
They will live apart in peace
The older will serve the younger
explanation: God told her two nations were in her womb. “and the older will serve the younger.” (Genesis 25:23, BSB)

content: Where did Hagar wander with her son after Abraham sent them away?
explanation: Abraham gave her bread and a skin of water. “She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.” (Genesis 21:14, BSB)

content: In Canaan, Abram traveled as far as the Oak of Moreh at which place?
explanation: There the LORD appeared to him. “as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem.” (Genesis 12:6, BSB)

content: In Canaan, Abram pitched his tent with Bethel to the west and which town to the east?
explanation: There he built another altar to the LORD. “with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east.” (Genesis 12:8, BSB)

content: Before Isaac was born, who did Abram say would inherit his house?
explanation: Abram had no child of his own yet. “and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?” (Genesis 15:2, BSB)

content: How long had Abram lived in Canaan when Sarai gave him Hagar as a wife?
explanation: Sarai still had no children. “So after he had lived in Canaan for ten years” (Genesis 16:3, BSB)

content: At what age did Abraham circumcise his son Isaac?
explanation: Abraham did as God had commanded him. “When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him” (Genesis 21:4, BSB)

content: How old was Abraham's wife Sarah when she died?
