explanation: She died in Hebron in the land of Canaan. “Now Sarah lived to be 127 years old.” (Genesis 23:1, BSB)

content: Where did Abraham bury his wife Sarah?
explanation: The cave was near Mamre, that is, Hebron. “Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre” (Genesis 23:19, BSB)

content: How many years did Abraham live in all?
explanation: He died old and contented. “Abraham lived a total of 175 years.” (Genesis 25:7, BSB)

content: How old was Isaac when he married Rebekah?
explanation: Rebekah was the sister of Laban the Aramean. “and Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah” (Genesis 25:20, BSB)

content: How old was Isaac when his twin sons Esau and Jacob were born?
explanation: Isaac had prayed for his wife because she was barren. “And Isaac was sixty years old when the twins were born.” (Genesis 25:26, BSB)

content: Looking for a wife for Isaac, Abraham's servant set out for Nahor's hometown in which region?
explanation: Abraham's relatives lived there. “And he set out for Nahor’s hometown in Aram-naharaim.” (Genesis 24:10, BSB)

content: When God promised Abraham a son by Sarah, how old did Abraham say Sarah was?
explanation: Abraham himself was nearly a hundred. “Can Sarah give birth at the age of ninety?” (Genesis 17:17, BSB)

content: On his way to Haran, what did Jacob use as a pillow when he slept?
explanation: He stopped for the night because the sun had set. “And taking one of the stones from that place, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.” (Genesis 28:11, BSB)

content: Sleeping on his way to Haran, what did Jacob dream about?
explanation: The ladder rested on the earth and reached heaven. “And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven” (Genesis 28:12, BSB)

content: In Jacob's dream on the way to Haran, who was going up and down the ladder?
explanation: At the top stood the LORD Himself. “and God’s angels were going up and down the ladder.” (Genesis 28:12, BSB)

content: In Jacob's ladder dream, what did God promise to do wherever Jacob went?
explanation: God promised to bring Jacob back to the land. “Look, I am with you, and I will watch over you wherever you go” (Genesis 28:15, BSB)

content: When Jacob woke from his ladder dream, what did he say about that place?
options: Surely the LORD is in this place
explanation: Jacob had not known God was there. “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it.” (Genesis 28:16, BSB)

content: After his ladder dream, what did Jacob do with the stone he had slept on?
options: Used it to build a house
Set it up as a pillar
explanation: He poured oil on it to mark the place. “and he set it up as a pillar. He poured oil on top of it” (Genesis 28:18, BSB)

content: What name did Jacob give the place where he dreamed of the ladder?
explanation: Bethel means house of God. “and he called that place Bethel” (Genesis 28:19, BSB)

content: The night before Jacob met Esau again, what happened when Jacob was left alone?
explanation: They wrestled through the night. “So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.” (Genesis 32:24, BSB)

content: On the night before meeting Esau, how long did the man wrestle with Jacob?
explanation: Jacob would not give up. “a man wrestled with him until daybreak.” (Genesis 32:24, BSB)

content: When the man he wrestled said, “Let me go,” what did Jacob answer?
explanation: Jacob wanted God's blessing. “I will not let you go unless you bless me.” (Genesis 32:26, BSB)

content: After wrestling all night, what new name was Jacob given?
explanation: He had struggled with God and with men and prevailed. “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel” (Genesis 32:28, BSB)

content: After wrestling with the man until daybreak, how did Jacob walk?
explanation: The man had struck his hip. “and he was limping because of his hip.” (Genesis 32:31, BSB)

content: Why did Jacob name the place where he wrestled Peniel?
options: He had seen God face to face
explanation: Jacob was amazed his life was spared. “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.” (Genesis 32:30, BSB)

content: When Isaac was old and ready to bless his son, what was wrong with his eyes?
options: They were too weak to see
explanation: Because he could not see, Jacob could trick him. “When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see” (Genesis 27:1, BSB)

content: When old Isaac planned to bless Esau, what did he first ask Esau to do?
explanation: Isaac wanted a tasty meal before giving the blessing. “go out into the field to hunt some game for me.” (Genesis 27:3, BSB)

content: To trick blind Isaac, what did Rebekah put on Jacob's hands and neck?
explanation: Esau was hairy, and Jacob was smooth. “She also put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.” (Genesis 27:16, BSB)

content: When blind Isaac touched Jacob, what did he say about the voice and the hands?
explanation: Isaac was unsure but blessed Jacob anyway. “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.” (Genesis 27:22, BSB)

content: When Esau planned to kill Jacob over the stolen blessing, where did Rebekah tell Jacob to flee?
options: To her brother Laban in Haran
explanation: She wanted Jacob safe until Esau calmed down. “flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.” (Genesis 27:43, BSB)

content: When Jacob reached Haran, who arrived at the well with her father's sheep?
explanation: Rachel was a shepherdess. “Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.” (Genesis 29:9, BSB)

content: When Jacob first saw Rachel at the well in Haran, what did he do for her?
options: Rolled the stone away, watered her sheep
explanation: Rachel was the daughter of his uncle Laban. “he went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle’s sheep.” (Genesis 29:10, BSB)

content: How many years did Jacob offer to work for Laban to marry Rachel?
explanation: Jacob loved Rachel. “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.” (Genesis 29:18, BSB)

content: How did Jacob's seven years of work for Rachel feel to him?
explanation: His love for her made the time fly. “yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.” (Genesis 29:20, BSB)

content: After working seven years for Rachel, whom did Jacob find he had married?
explanation: Laban had tricked Jacob. “When morning came, there was Leah!” (Genesis 29:25, BSB)

content: What were the names of Laban's two daughters?
explanation: Leah was older and Rachel was younger. “the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.” (Genesis 29:16, BSB)

content: What did Rachel name her first son?
explanation: God remembered Rachel and gave her a son. “She named him Joseph” (Genesis 30:24, BSB)

content: When Jacob returned home, how many men were coming with Esau to meet him?
explanation: Jacob was greatly afraid. “he and four hundred men with him.” (Genesis 32:6, BSB)

content: When Esau finally met Jacob again after many years, what did Esau do?
explanation: The brothers wept together. “Esau, however, ran to him and embraced him” (Genesis 33:4, BSB)

content: As Jacob approached Esau after many years apart, how many times did he bow to the ground?
explanation: Jacob came humbly to his brother. “and bowed to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.” (Genesis 33:3, BSB)

content: As Rachel was dying in childbirth, what name did Jacob give her newborn son?
explanation: Rachel had named him Ben-oni. “But his father called him Benjamin.” (Genesis 35:18, BSB)

content: How many sons did Jacob have in all?
explanation: They became the twelve tribes of Israel. “Jacob had twelve sons:” (Genesis 35:22, BSB)

content: What did Isaac name the well that no one quarreled over?
explanation: Isaac said the LORD had made room for them. “He named it Rehoboth” (Genesis 26:22, BSB)

content: Before Jacob named it Bethel, what was that city called?
explanation: Jacob renamed it after his ladder dream. “though previously the city had been named Luz.” (Genesis 28:19, BSB)

content: At Bethel, how much of all God gave him did Jacob vow to give back?
explanation: Jacob made a vow after his dream. “and of all that You give me I will surely give You a tenth.” (Genesis 28:22, BSB)

content: Which servant girl did Laban give to his daughter Leah as her maidservant?
explanation: Bilhah was given to Rachel. “And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.” (Genesis 29:24, BSB)

content: How many years in all did Jacob serve in Laban's household?
explanation: Fourteen years for his wives and six for his flocks. “Thus for twenty years I have served in your household” (Genesis 31:41, BSB)

content: Jacob complained that his uncle Laban had changed his wages how many times?
explanation: Laban kept cheating Jacob. “and you have changed my wages ten times!” (Genesis 31:41, BSB)

content: When angels met Jacob on his way home, what did he name that place?
explanation: He called it the camp of God. “So he named that place Mahanaim.” (Genesis 32:2, BSB)

content: The night before meeting Esau, which stream did Jacob's family cross?
explanation: Then Jacob was left alone. “and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.” (Genesis 32:22, BSB)

content: Where was Jacob's wife Rachel buried?
explanation: Ephrath is Bethlehem. “So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).” (Genesis 35:19, BSB)

content: Who was Jacob's firstborn son?
explanation: Reuben was Leah's first son. “The sons of Leah were Reuben the firstborn of Jacob” (Genesis 35:23, BSB)

content: What special gift did Jacob make for his son Joseph?
explanation: Jacob loved Joseph more than his other sons. “so he made him a robe of many colors.” (Genesis 37:3, BSB)

content: Why did Joseph's brothers hate him?
explanation: They could not even speak a kind word to him. “When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him” (Genesis 37:4, BSB)

content: In young Joseph's first dream, what bowed down to his sheaf of grain?
explanation: His brothers hated him even more after this dream. “while your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.” (Genesis 37:7, BSB)

content: In young Joseph's second dream, what was bowing down to him?
options: The sun, moon, and eleven stars
explanation: Even his father wondered about this dream. “the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.” (Genesis 37:9, BSB)

content: When Joseph's brothers saw him coming in the fields, what did they call him?
explanation: They were angry about his dreams. ““Here comes that dreamer!” they said to one another.” (Genesis 37:19, BSB)

content: After taking his colorful robe, where did Joseph's brothers throw him?
explanation: The pit had no water in it. “and they took him and threw him into the pit. Now the pit was empty, with no water in it.” (Genesis 37:24, BSB)

content: Who did Joseph's jealous brothers sell him to?
explanation: The traders took Joseph to Egypt. “and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt.” (Genesis 37:28, BSB)

content: After selling Joseph, what did his brothers dip his robe in to fool their father?
explanation: They wanted Jacob to think an animal had killed Joseph. “slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in its blood.” (Genesis 37:31, BSB)

content: In Pharaoh's first dream, what came up out of the Nile?
explanation: Then seven thin cows came up after them. “when seven cows, sleek and well-fed, came up from the river” (Genesis 41:2, BSB)

content: In Pharaoh's dream by the Nile, what did the thin cows do to the fat cows?
explanation: Then Pharaoh woke up troubled. “And the cows that were sickly and thin devoured the seven sleek, well-fed cows.” (Genesis 41:4, BSB)

content: When Pharaoh asked Joseph to explain his dream, who did Joseph say would give the answer?
explanation: Joseph gave God the credit. “but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer.” (Genesis 41:16, BSB)

content: Joseph said Pharaoh's dreams meant seven years of plenty followed by what?
explanation: Egypt needed to store food during the good years. “but seven years of famine will follow them.” (Genesis 41:30, BSB)

content: After Joseph explained the dreams, what did Pharaoh put him in charge of?
explanation: Pharaoh saw that God's Spirit was in Joseph. “I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.” (Genesis 41:41, BSB)

content: When Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of Egypt, what did he put on Joseph's finger?
explanation: The ring showed Joseph had Pharaoh's authority. “Then Pharaoh removed the signet ring from his finger, put it on Joseph’s finger” (Genesis 41:42, BSB)

content: During the great famine, why did every nation come to Joseph in Egypt?
explanation: Joseph had stored grain during the good years. “And every nation came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain” (Genesis 41:57, BSB)

content: When Joseph finally told his brothers in Egypt who he was, what did he say?
explanation: He also asked if his father was still alive. “Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?”” (Genesis 45:3, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: When Joseph revealed who he was, how did his brothers feel?
explanation: They could not even answer him. “because they were terrified in his presence.” (Genesis 45:3, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: When Joseph made himself known to his brothers, how loudly did he weep?
explanation: Even Pharaoh's household heard about it. “But he wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him” (Genesis 45:2, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: Joseph told his brothers that God sent him to Egypt ahead of them for what reason?
explanation: Joseph saw God's plan in all that happened. “because it was to save lives that God sent me before you.” (Genesis 45:5, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: Joseph told his brothers who had really sent him to Egypt. Who?
explanation: God had made him ruler over Egypt. “Therefore it was not you who sent me here, but God” (Genesis 45:8, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: In which region of Egypt did Joseph invite his family to settle?
explanation: There they could be near Joseph. “You shall settle in the land of Goshen and be near me” (Genesis 45:10, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: When old Jacob heard that Joseph was alive, what did he decide?
options: To go see him before he died
explanation: Jacob had mourned Joseph for many years. “My son Joseph is still alive! I will go to see him before I die.” (Genesis 45:28, BSB)
tags: Joseph Makes Himself Known to His Brothers

content: How old was Joseph when he was tending the flock with his brothers?
explanation: He brought his father a bad report about his brothers. “When Joseph was seventeen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers” (Genesis 37:2, BSB)

content: Which brother tried to save Joseph by telling the others to throw him in a pit instead of killing him?
explanation: Reuben planned to bring Joseph back to their father. “Reuben said this so that he could rescue Joseph from their hands and return him to his father.” (Genesis 37:22, BSB)

content: Which brother suggested selling Joseph instead of killing him?
explanation: He said there was no profit in killing their brother. “Then Judah said to his brothers, “What profit will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?” (Genesis 37:26, BSB)

content: For how much silver did Joseph's brothers sell him?
explanation: The traders took Joseph down to Egypt. “and sold him for twenty shekels of silver” (Genesis 37:28, BSB)

content: In Egypt, who bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites?
explanation: Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh. “an Egyptian named Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him” (Genesis 39:1, BSB)

content: Why did Joseph succeed while serving in Potiphar's house?
explanation: Potiphar put him in charge of everything he owned. “And the LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man” (Genesis 39:2, BSB)

content: When Potiphar's wife grabbed Joseph by his cloak, what did Joseph do?
options: Left the cloak and ran outside
explanation: Joseph refused to sin against God. “But leaving his cloak in her hand, he escaped and ran outside.” (Genesis 39:12, BSB)

content: While Joseph was in prison, what did the warden put him in charge of?
explanation: The LORD gave Joseph success even in prison. “And the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph’s care” (Genesis 39:22, BSB)

content: Which two officers of Pharaoh ended up in prison with Joseph?
options: The chief cupbearer and chief baker
The chief priest and a scribe
explanation: Pharaoh was angry with them. “the chief cupbearer and the chief baker” (Genesis 40:2, BSB)

content: In prison, Joseph said the three branches in the cupbearer's dream meant what?
explanation: In three days the cupbearer got his job back. “The three branches are three days.” (Genesis 40:12, BSB)

content: After the cupbearer was set free from prison, what did he do about Joseph?
explanation: Joseph stayed in prison two more years. “The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him.” (Genesis 40:23, BSB)

content: In Pharaoh's second dream, what had scorched the thin heads of grain?
explanation: The thin heads swallowed the plump ones. “thin and scorched by the east wind.” (Genesis 41:6, BSB)

content: How old was Joseph when he entered Pharaoh's service?
explanation: Thirteen years had passed since he was sold. “Now Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt.” (Genesis 41:46, BSB)

content: What did Joseph name his firstborn son in Egypt?
explanation: Joseph said God had made him forget his hardship. “Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh” (Genesis 41:51, BSB)

content: During the famine, how many of Joseph's brothers first went to Egypt to buy grain?
explanation: Benjamin stayed home with Jacob. “So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.” (Genesis 42:3, BSB)

content: Which brother did Jacob keep at home when the others first went to Egypt for grain?
explanation: Jacob was afraid harm might come to him. “But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers” (Genesis 42:4, BSB)

content: When Joseph's brothers came to Egypt to buy grain, did they recognize him?
explanation: Joseph recognized them, but he looked like an Egyptian ruler. “Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.” (Genesis 42:8, BSB)

content: Which of his brothers did Joseph keep bound in Egypt?
explanation: The others had to go home and bring Benjamin. “he took Simeon from them and had him bound before their eyes.” (Genesis 42:24, BSB)

content: Whose grain sack did Joseph order his silver cup to be hidden in?
explanation: The youngest brother was Benjamin. “Put my cup, the silver one, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack” (Genesis 44:2, BSB)

content: At the end of Genesis, what did Joseph tell his brothers about the evil they had planned against him?
explanation: God used it to save many lives. “As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good” (Genesis 50:20, BSB)

content: When Jacob came down to Egypt, what did Joseph do when he met his father?
explanation: Father and son were together again after many years. “Joseph presented himself to him, embraced him, and wept profusely.” (Genesis 46:29, BSB)

content: When Joseph was sold, what were the traders' camels carrying down to Egypt?
explanation: The caravan was coming from Gilead. “Their camels were carrying spices, balm, and myrrh on their way down to Egypt.” (Genesis 37:25, BSB)

content: What was Potiphar's position in Egypt?
explanation: He was an officer of Pharaoh. “an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.” (Genesis 37:36, BSB)

content: In the chief baker's dream in prison, how many baskets were on his head?
explanation: Joseph said the three baskets were three days. “There were three baskets of white bread on my head.” (Genesis 40:16, BSB)

content: On what occasion were Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker brought out of prison?
explanation: Pharaoh held a feast for all his officials. “On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday” (Genesis 40:20, BSB)

content: How long after the cupbearer's release did Pharaoh have his troubling dream?
explanation: Then the cupbearer finally remembered Joseph. “After two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream” (Genesis 41:1, BSB)

content: What Egyptian name did Pharaoh give Joseph?
explanation: Joseph took charge of all the land of Egypt. “Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah” (Genesis 41:45, BSB)

content: Whom did Pharaoh give Joseph as his wife?
explanation: Her father was priest of On. “and he gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife.” (Genesis 41:45, BSB)

content: What did Joseph name his second son in Egypt?
explanation: Joseph said God had made him fruitful. “And the second son he named Ephraim” (Genesis 41:52, BSB)

content: When Jacob met Pharaoh in Egypt, how old did he say he was?
explanation: Jacob said his years had been few and hard. ““My travels have lasted 130 years,” Jacob replied.” (Genesis 47:9, BSB)

content: How old was Jacob when his life ended in Egypt?
explanation: He lived seventeen years in Egypt. “and the length of his life was 147 years.” (Genesis 47:28, BSB)

content: How old was Joseph when he died in Egypt?
explanation: His body was placed in a coffin in Egypt. “So Joseph died at the age of 110.” (Genesis 50:26, BSB)

content: In Jacob's blessing of his sons, from which son would the scepter not depart?
explanation: Kings would come from Judah's line. “The scepter will not depart from Judah” (Genesis 49:10, BSB)

content: When Joseph rode in Pharaoh's second chariot, what did men call out before him?
explanation: Joseph was placed over all Egypt. “with men calling out before him, “Bow the knee!”” (Genesis 41:43, BSB)

content: Which great city did God send the prophet Jonah to preach against?
explanation: Its wickedness had come up before God. “Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it” (Jonah 1:2, BSB)

content: Instead of obeying God's call to Nineveh, where did Jonah try to run?
explanation: He tried to get away from the LORD. “Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish” (Jonah 1:3, BSB)

content: What did the LORD send on the sea while Jonah was running away?
explanation: The ship was about to break apart. “such a violent storm arose that the ship was in danger of breaking apart.” (Jonah 1:4, BSB)

content: During the storm at sea, what was Jonah doing below deck?
explanation: The captain had to wake him up. “where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.” (Jonah 1:5, BSB)

content: How did the sailors find out Jonah was the cause of the storm?
explanation: The lot fell on Jonah. “So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.” (Jonah 1:7, BSB)

content: During the storm, what did Jonah tell the sailors to do to calm the sea?
explanation: Jonah knew the storm was his fault. “and cast me into the sea, so it may quiet down for you.” (Jonah 1:12, BSB)

content: What did the LORD appoint to swallow Jonah in the sea?
explanation: God saved Jonah's life this way. “Now the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah” (Jonah 1:17, BSB)

content: How long was Jonah inside the belly of the great fish?
explanation: Jesus later spoke of this sign. “and Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish.” (Jonah 1:17, BSB)

content: When Jonah finally preached in Nineveh, how did the people respond?
explanation: Everyone put on sackcloth. “And the Ninevites believed God. They proclaimed a fast and dressed in sackcloth” (Jonah 3:5, BSB)

content: When God spared the city of Nineveh, how did Jonah feel?
explanation: Jonah did not want God to show them mercy. “Jonah, however, was greatly displeased, and he became angry.” (Jonah 4:1, BSB)

content: After preaching to Nineveh, where did Jonah sit to watch what would happen?
options: In a shelter east of the city
explanation: He waited to see if the city would be destroyed. “Then Jonah left the city and sat down east of it, where he made himself a shelter” (Jonah 4:5, BSB)

content: Outside Nineveh, what did God make grow to give Jonah shade?
explanation: Jonah was very pleased with it. “So the LORD God appointed a vine, and it grew up to provide shade over Jonah’s head” (Jonah 4:6, BSB)

content: What did God send to make Jonah's shade plant wither?
explanation: The plant died the next day. “God appointed a worm that attacked the plant so that it withered.” (Jonah 4:7, BSB)

content: After Jonah's shade plant withered, what beat down on his head?
explanation: Jonah grew faint. “and the sun beat down on Jonah’s head so that he grew faint” (Jonah 4:8, BSB)

content: At the end of Jonah's story, what did God say He cared about?
explanation: God cares even for Israel's enemies. “So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh” (Jonah 4:11, BSB)

content: From which port did Jonah board a ship to run from God?
explanation: He paid the fare to sail for Tarshish. “He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish.” (Jonah 1:3, BSB)

content: In the storm on Jonah's ship, what did the frightened sailors throw overboard first?
explanation: They tried to lighten the load. “And they threw the ship’s cargo into the sea to lighten the load.” (Jonah 1:5, BSB)

content: When the sailors asked who he was, what did Jonah say he was?
explanation: He worshiped the God who made sea and land. ““I am a Hebrew,” replied Jonah.” (Jonah 1:9, BSB)

content: What happened when the sailors threw Jonah into the sea?
explanation: The sailors then feared the LORD. “and the raging sea grew calm.” (Jonah 1:15, BSB)

content: Where was Jonah when he prayed to the LORD his God?
explanation: He cried out to God from the deep. “From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God” (Jonah 2:1, BSB)

content: What did the great fish do when the LORD commanded it?
explanation: Jonah got a second chance. “and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.” (Jonah 2:10, BSB)

content: What warning did Jonah proclaim in Nineveh?
options: Repent or the sea will rise
Forty days and Nineveh will fall
explanation: He walked through the city calling it out. “Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!” (Jonah 3:4, BSB)

content: When the king of Nineveh heard Jonah's warning, what did he do?
explanation: Even the king humbled himself. “covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.” (Jonah 3:6, BSB)

content: When God saw Nineveh turn from its evil ways, what did He do?
explanation: God shows mercy to those who repent. “He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.” (Jonah 3:10, BSB)

content: Why did Jonah say he had fled toward Tarshish in the first place?
options: He was afraid of the sea
explanation: He did not want Nineveh to be spared. “I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God” (Jonah 4:2, BSB)

content: Who was the father of the prophet Jonah?
explanation: The book opens with his name. “Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai” (Jonah 1:1, BSB)

content: How long a journey was it to cross the great city of Nineveh?
explanation: It was an exceedingly great city. “requiring a three-day journey.” (Jonah 3:3, BSB)

content: How many people did God say lived in Nineveh who could not tell right hand from left?
explanation: There were many cattle as well. “which has more than 120,000 people” (Jonah 4:11, BSB)

content: What kind of wind did God send on Jonah after his shade plant withered?
explanation: Jonah wished to die. “God appointed a scorching east wind” (Jonah 4:8, BSB)

content: In the king of Nineveh's decree, who had to go without food or water?
explanation: The whole city fasted. “Let no man or beast, herd or flock, taste anything at all.” (Jonah 3:7, BSB)

content: Proverbs says to trust in the LORD with how much of your heart?
explanation: God wants our full trust. “Trust in the LORD with all your heart” (Proverbs 3:5, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs tells us not to lean on what?
explanation: Our own understanding is limited. “and lean not on your own understanding” (Proverbs 3:5, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says if you acknowledge God in all your ways, He will do what?
explanation: God guides those who trust Him. “and He will make your paths straight.” (Proverbs 3:6, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs warns us not to be wise in whose eyes?
explanation: Instead, fear the LORD and turn from evil. “Be not wise in your own eyes” (Proverbs 3:7, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says to honor the LORD with your wealth and with what?
explanation: God deserves our first and best. “Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your harvest” (Proverbs 3:9, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says the LORD disciplines whom?
explanation: Like a father who delights in his son. “for the LORD disciplines the one He loves” (Proverbs 3:12, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs tells a son not to reject what from the LORD?
explanation: God's correction is a sign of His love. “My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD” (Proverbs 3:11, BSB)
tags: Trust in the Lord with All Your Heart

content: Proverbs says a true friend loves when?
explanation: Real friends stay through hard times. “A friend loves at all times” (Proverbs 17:17, BSB)

content: Proverbs says what kind of answer turns away anger?
explanation: Kind words calm people down. “A gentle answer turns away wrath” (Proverbs 15:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs tells the lazy person to learn from which creature?
explanation: The ant works hard without being told. “Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker” (Proverbs 6:6, BSB)

content: Proverbs says what goes before destruction?
explanation: A haughty spirit comes before a fall. “Pride goes before destruction” (Proverbs 16:18, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a child trained in the way he should go will do what when he is old?
explanation: Good training lasts a lifetime. “Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.” (Proverbs 22:6, BSB)

content: In its opening chapter, Proverbs says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of what?
explanation: Fools despise wisdom and discipline. “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge” (Proverbs 1:7, BSB)

content: Proverbs says to guard what with all diligence, because springs of life flow from it?
explanation: What is in the heart shapes all of life. “Guard your heart with all diligence” (Proverbs 4:23, BSB)

content: Proverbs says what is detestable to the LORD?
explanation: Those who deal faithfully are His delight. “Lying lips are detestable to the LORD” (Proverbs 12:22, BSB)

content: Proverbs says to commit what to the LORD so that your plans succeed?
explanation: Then your plans will be achieved. “Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.” (Proverbs 16:3, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a joyful heart is good what?
explanation: A broken spirit dries up the bones. “A joyful heart is good medicine” (Proverbs 17:22, BSB)

content: Proverbs calls the name of the LORD a strong what?
explanation: The righteous run to it for safety. “The name of the LORD is a strong tower” (Proverbs 18:10, BSB)

content: Proverbs says as iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens whom?
explanation: Friends help each other grow. “As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.” (Proverbs 27:17, BSB)

content: Proverbs says every word of God is what?
explanation: He is a shield to those who trust Him. “Every word of God is flawless” (Proverbs 30:5, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a wife of noble character is far more precious than what?
explanation: Her worth is beyond price. “She is far more precious than rubies.” (Proverbs 31:10, BSB)

content: Proverbs says charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but who is to be praised?
options: A woman who fears the LORD
explanation: Character matters more than looks. “but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.” (Proverbs 31:30, BSB)

content: Proverbs says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of what?
explanation: Knowing the Holy One is understanding. “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom” (Proverbs 9:10, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a wise son brings joy to whom?
explanation: A foolish son brings grief to his mother. “A wise son brings joy to his father” (Proverbs 10:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a brother is born for what?
explanation: Family helps in hard times. “and a brother is born for adversity.” (Proverbs 17:17, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a harsh word does what?
explanation: A gentle answer turns away wrath. “but a harsh word stirs up anger.” (Proverbs 15:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a haughty spirit comes before what?
explanation: Pride goes before destruction. “and a haughty spirit before a fall.” (Proverbs 16:18, BSB)

content: Proverbs says a word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of what?
explanation: The right word at the right time is beautiful. “A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.” (Proverbs 25:11, BSB)

content: Proverbs compares a fool repeating his folly to what?
options: A dog returning to its vomit
explanation: Fools keep making the same mistakes. “As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.” (Proverbs 26:11, BSB)

content: Proverbs says which small creatures make their homes in the rocks?
explanation: They are weak but wise. “the rock badgers are creatures of little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks” (Proverbs 30:26, BSB)

content: Proverbs says which creatures have no king, yet advance in formation?
explanation: They work together without a ruler. “the locusts have no king, yet they all advance in formation” (Proverbs 30:27, BSB)

content: Proverbs says which creature can be caught in the hand, yet is found in kings' palaces?
explanation: Small things can go far. “and the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.” (Proverbs 30:28, BSB)

content: Proverbs says the ants, though weak, do what in the summer?
explanation: They plan ahead. “yet they store up their food in the summer” (Proverbs 30:25, BSB)

content: Whose proverbs begin the section that says a wise son brings joy to his father?
explanation: Solomon wrote many proverbs. “The proverbs of Solomon” (Proverbs 10:1, BSB)

content: Proverbs says the righteous run to the name of the LORD and are what?
explanation: His name is a strong tower. “the righteous run to it and are safe.” (Proverbs 18:10, BSB)

content: Complete the start of David's famous psalm: “The LORD is my…”
explanation: God cares for His people like a shepherd. “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.” (Psalm 23:1, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, where does the LORD make him lie down?
explanation: The Shepherd gives rest. “He makes me lie down in green pastures” (Psalm 23:2, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, beside what does the LORD lead him?
explanation: The Shepherd leads to peaceful places. “He leads me beside quiet waters.” (Psalm 23:2, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, what does the LORD restore?
explanation: God refreshes us from the inside. “He restores my soul” (Psalm 23:3, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, why does he fear no evil in the dark valley?
explanation: God's presence takes away fear. “I will fear no evil, for You are with me” (Psalm 23:4, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, which two things comfort him?
explanation: A shepherd uses them to guide and protect. “Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.” (Psalm 23:4, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, what will follow him all the days of his life?
explanation: He will dwell in the house of the LORD forever. “Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life” (Psalm 23:6, BSB)

content: In David's shepherd psalm, what happens to his cup?
explanation: God blesses him more than enough. “my cup overflows.” (Psalm 23:5, BSB)

content: In the very first psalm, what does the blessed man delight in?
explanation: He loves God's word. “But his delight is in the Law of the LORD” (Psalm 1:2, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, when does the blessed man meditate on God's law?
explanation: God's word fills his thoughts. “and on His law he meditates day and night.” (Psalm 1:2, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, the blessed man is like what?
explanation: He grows strong and bears fruit. “He is like a tree planted by streams of water” (Psalm 1:3, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, what are the wicked like?
explanation: They have nothing that lasts. “For they are like chaff driven off by the wind.” (Psalm 1:4, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, the blessed man does not sit in the seat of whom?
explanation: He avoids the company of scoffers. “or sit in the seat of mockers.” (Psalm 1:1, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, what does the LORD guard?
explanation: The way of the wicked will perish. “For the LORD guards the path of the righteous” (Psalm 1:6, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the very first psalm, what happens to the leaf of the tree by the streams?
explanation: The blessed man prospers in all he does. “whose leaf does not wither” (Psalm 1:3, BSB)
tags: Blessed Is the One Who Delights in God's Law

content: In the longest psalm, God's word is called a lamp to what?
explanation: God's word shows us where to step. “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.” (Psalm 119:105, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, God's word is called a light to what?
explanation: It guides the whole way ahead. “a light to my path.” (Psalm 119:105, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, where did the writer hide God's word?
explanation: Knowing God's word helps us resist sin. “I have hidden Your word in my heart that I might not sin against You.” (Psalm 119:11, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, how can a young person keep his way pure?
options: By guarding it with God's word
explanation: God's word keeps young people on the right path. “How can a young man keep his way pure? By guarding it according to Your word.” (Psalm 119:9, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, God's words taste sweeter than what?
explanation: The writer loved God's words. “sweeter than honey in my mouth!” (Psalm 119:103, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In the longest psalm, why did the writer hide God's word in his heart?
explanation: God's word protects us from sin. “that I might not sin against You.” (Psalm 119:11, BSB)
tags: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet

content: In a psalm of David, what do the heavens declare?
explanation: Creation shows how great God is. “The heavens declare the glory of God” (Psalm 19:1, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, what do his enemies do to get his clothing?
explanation: The Gospels saw this happen at Jesus' cross. “They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.” (Psalm 22:18, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, the LORD is called his light and his what?
explanation: So David asks, whom shall I fear? “The LORD is my light and my salvation” (Psalm 27:1, BSB)

content: A psalm invites us to taste and see what?
explanation: Blessed is the one who takes refuge in Him. “Taste and see that the LORD is good” (Psalm 34:8, BSB)

content: A psalm says if you delight yourself in the LORD, He will give you what?
explanation: Delighting in God shapes what we desire. “Delight yourself in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart.” (Psalm 37:4, BSB)

content: A psalm says the soul longs for God as a deer pants for what?
explanation: The writer thirsts for God. “As the deer pants for streams of water” (Psalm 42:1, BSB)

content: A psalm calls God our refuge and what?
explanation: He is an ever-present help in trouble. “God is our refuge and strength” (Psalm 46:1, BSB)

content: In a psalm, what does God tell us to be, so we know that He is God?
explanation: God will be exalted among the nations. “Be still and know that I am God” (Psalm 46:10, BSB)

content: In David's psalm of repentance, what does he ask God to create in him?
explanation: David wanted to be made right with God. “Create in me a clean heart, O God” (Psalm 51:10, BSB)

content: A psalm of thanksgiving tells all the earth to make what to the LORD?
explanation: Worship can be loud and glad. “Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth.” (Psalm 100:1, BSB)

content: A psalm of thanksgiving says we are God's people and the sheep of what?
explanation: God made us and we belong to Him. “we are His people, and the sheep of His pasture.” (Psalm 100:3, BSB)

content: A psalm of thanksgiving says to enter God's gates with what?
explanation: And His courts with praise. “Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise” (Psalm 100:4, BSB)

content: A psalm says God removes our sins from us as far as what?
options: The east is from the west
The sky is from the sea
explanation: God's forgiveness is complete. “As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.” (Psalm 103:12, BSB)

content: A psalm says: This is the day that the LORD has made; we will do what?
options: Rejoice and be glad in it
explanation: Every day is a gift from God. “This is the day that the LORD has made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.” (Psalm 118:24, BSB)

content: In a song of ascents, where does the writer say his help comes from?
options: The LORD, Maker of heaven and earth
explanation: He lifts his eyes beyond the hills to God. “My help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.” (Psalm 121:2, BSB)

content: A song of ascents says the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor what?
explanation: God never stops watching over His people. “the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.” (Psalm 121:4, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, how does he say he was made?
explanation: David praised God for how He made him. “for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” (Psalm 139:14, BSB)

content: The very last psalm calls on everything that has breath to do what?
explanation: The book of Psalms ends in praise. “Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!” (Psalm 150:6, BSB)

content: A psalm says God will command His angels to do what for you?
options: Guard you in all your ways
explanation: God protects those who trust Him. “For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.” (Psalm 91:11, BSB)

content: A song of ascents says how good and pleasant it is when brothers do what?
explanation: Unity among God's people is a blessing. “how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony!” (Psalm 133:1, BSB)

content: A psalm says the length of our days is seventy years, or how many if we are strong?
explanation: Life passes quickly. “The length of our days is seventy years— or eighty if we are strong” (Psalm 90:10, BSB)

content: A psalm says that in God's sight a thousand years are like what?
explanation: God is not limited by time. “For in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes” (Psalm 90:4, BSB)

content: In a psalm of the exile, by which rivers did God's people sit and weep?
explanation: They wept when they remembered Zion. “By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.” (Psalm 137:1, BSB)

content: In the psalm of the exiles in Babylon, where did they hang their harps?
explanation: They were too sad to sing. “There on the willows we hung our harps” (Psalm 137:2, BSB)

content: The psalm about a deer panting for water is a Maskil of whom?
explanation: The sons of Korah wrote several psalms. “A Maskil of the sons of Korah.” (Psalm 42:1, BSB)

content: To which tune was the psalm “My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?” set?
explanation: It is a psalm of David for the choirmaster. “To the tune of “The Doe of the Dawn.”” (Psalm 22:1, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, the heavens are called the work of what?
explanation: David wondered why God cares for people. “When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers” (Psalm 8:3, BSB)

content: In the shortest psalm, who is called to praise the LORD?
explanation: God's love reaches every people. “Praise the LORD, all you nations!” (Psalm 117:1, BSB)

content: In a psalm of David, where did God knit him together?
explanation: God formed him before he was born. “You knit me together in my mother’s womb.” (Psalm 139:13, BSB)

content: In the days of the judges, why did Naomi's family leave Bethlehem?
explanation: There was not enough food in the land. “there was a famine in the land.” (Ruth 1:1, BSB)

content: During the famine, where did Naomi's family go to live?
explanation: There her sons married Moabite women. “went to reside in the land of Moab.” (Ruth 1:1, BSB)

content: When Naomi told her to go home, what did Ruth promise her?
options: I will go back to Moab
Wherever you go, I will go
explanation: Ruth would not leave her mother-in-law. “For wherever you go, I will go” (Ruth 1:16, BSB)

content: Ruth told Naomi, “Your people will be my people, and your God will be…” what?
explanation: Ruth chose to follow the God of Israel. “your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.” (Ruth 1:16, BSB)

content: When Naomi urged her daughters-in-law to go home, what did Orpah do?
explanation: But Ruth clung to Naomi. “and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.” (Ruth 1:14, BSB)

content: In Bethlehem, what did Ruth go into the fields to do?
explanation: Poor people gathered leftover grain after the harvesters. “Please let me go into the fields and glean heads of grain” (Ruth 2:2, BSB)

content: In Bethlehem, whose field did Ruth happen to glean in?
explanation: Boaz was from the clan of Naomi's husband. “And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz” (Ruth 2:3, BSB)

content: Why was Boaz so kind to Ruth in his field?
options: She had been kind to Naomi
explanation: He had heard how she left her own land for Naomi. “I have been made fully aware of all you have done for your mother-in-law” (Ruth 2:11, BSB)

content: At the end of the book of Ruth, whom did Ruth marry?
explanation: The LORD gave them a son. “So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife.” (Ruth 4:13, BSB)

content: Ruth's son Obed became the grandfather of which famous king?
explanation: A Moabite woman became part of King David's family. “He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.” (Ruth 4:17, BSB)

content: In the book of Ruth, what was the name of Naomi's husband?
explanation: He died in Moab. “The man’s name was Elimelech, his wife’s name was Naomi” (Ruth 1:2, BSB)

content: What were the names of Naomi's two Moabite daughters-in-law?
explanation: Both were women of Moab. “one named Orpah and the other named Ruth.” (Ruth 1:4, BSB)

content: When Naomi came back to Bethlehem, what did she ask the women to call her instead?
explanation: She felt the Almighty had dealt bitterly with her. “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20, BSB)

content: Naomi said she went away full, but the LORD brought her back how?
explanation: She had lost her husband and both sons. “I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty.” (Ruth 1:21, BSB)

content: At what time of year did Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem?
explanation: It was the right time for Ruth to glean. “And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.” (Ruth 1:22, BSB)

content: How was Boaz related to Naomi?
options: A relative on her husband's side
explanation: He was from the clan of Elimelech. “Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side” (Ruth 2:1, BSB)

content: In his field, what did Boaz tell Ruth to do when she was thirsty?
options: Drink from the young men's jars
explanation: Boaz made sure she was cared for. “And when you are thirsty, go and drink from the jars the young men have filled.” (Ruth 2:9, BSB)

content: When Boaz showed her kindness, what did Ruth say she was?
explanation: She was amazed he noticed her. “even though I am a foreigner?” (Ruth 2:10, BSB)

content: Boaz told Ruth she had taken refuge under whose wings?
options: The LORD's, the God of Israel
explanation: Ruth had come to trust Israel's God. “under whose wings you have taken refuge.” (Ruth 2:12, BSB)

content: What did Naomi tell Ruth that Boaz was to their family?
explanation: A kinsman-redeemer could buy back family land. “He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.” (Ruth 2:20, BSB)

content: Where was Boaz winnowing barley the night Ruth went to see him?
explanation: Naomi told Ruth where to find him. “tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.” (Ruth 3:2, BSB)

content: On the threshing floor, what did Ruth ask Boaz to spread over her?
explanation: She was asking him to redeem her as a kinsman. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer.” (Ruth 3:9, BSB)

content: Where did Boaz sit down to settle the matter of redeeming Naomi's land?
explanation: Legal matters were settled at the gate. “Meanwhile, Boaz went to the gate and sat down there.” (Ruth 4:1, BSB)

content: In old Israel, how did a man make a land deal legally binding?
options: Removed his sandal and gave it
explanation: This was a confirmation in Israel. “a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party” (Ruth 4:7, BSB)

content: What was the name of the son born to Ruth and Boaz?
explanation: He became King David's grandfather. “and they named him Obed.” (Ruth 4:17, BSB)

content: What were the names of Naomi's two sons?
explanation: Both sons died in Moab. “and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion.” (Ruth 1:2, BSB)

content: About how long had Naomi's family lived in Moab when her sons died?
explanation: Naomi was left without husband or sons. “And after they had lived in Moab about ten years” (Ruth 1:4, BSB)

content: How much barley did Ruth gather on her first day in Boaz's field?
explanation: She worked in the field until evening. “it was about an ephah of barley.” (Ruth 2:17, BSB)

content: Why did the closer kinsman-redeemer refuse to redeem Naomi's land?
options: It would jeopardize his own inheritance
explanation: So Boaz became the redeemer. “or I would jeopardize my own inheritance.” (Ruth 4:6, BSB)

content: At the city gate, Boaz said Ruth was the widow of which man?
explanation: Boaz kept the dead man's name alive in Israel. “I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife” (Ruth 4:10, BSB)

content: Naomi's family were Ephrathites from which town?
explanation: They returned there after the famine. “They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah” (Ruth 1:2, BSB)

content: Who gave Ruth's baby the name Obed?
explanation: They said a son had been born to Naomi. “The neighbor women said, “A son has been born to Naomi,” and they named him Obed.” (Ruth 4:17, BSB)
